gene.name: alpha 1,4-galactosyltransferase (P1PK blood group)
gene.function: Glycosyltransferase involved in biosynthesis of P1, P(k) and the rare NOR antigens of P1PK histo-blood group system. Catalyzes the transfer of galactose from UDP-alpha-D-galactose in an alpha1,4 linkage to lactosylceramide/beta-D-galactosyl-(1->4)-beta-D-glucosyl-(1<->1)- ceramide(d18:1(4E)) to produce globotriaosylceramide/globoside Gb3Cer (d18:1(4E)), also known as P(k) antigen or CD77. Globoside Gb3Cer/P(k)/CD77 is a root structure in biosynthesis pathway of neutral glycosphingolipids of the globo-series. Broadly expressed in cell membranes of immune cells and other tissues, Gb3Cer/P(k)/CD77 antigen may participate in mechanisms that regulate cell-cell interactions and cell differentiation. In germinal center B cells, Gb3Cer/CD77 interacts with CD19 to drive centroblast-to-centrocyte transition, B cell receptor complex assembly and T follicular helper cell differentiation. In epithelium, Gb3Cer regulates CDH1/E-cadherin- dependent cell-cell adhesion counteracting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (By similarity). Synthesizes P1 glycan epitope (alpha-D-Gal-(1->4)-beta-D-Gal-(1->4)-GlcNAc-R) by transferring a galactose moiety to paragloboside nLc4 or to complex-type N-glycans. Generates the rare NOR1 and NOR2 antigens which carry a Gal(alpha1->4)GalNAc terminal moiety and are both derived from Gb4Cer precursor. Also able to transfer galactose to galactosylceramide/beta-D-Gal-(1<->1')-Cer.

gene.name: acetyl-CoA carboxylase alpha
gene.function: Cytosolic enzyme that catalyzes the carboxylation of acetyl- CoA to malonyl-CoA, the first and rate-limiting step of de novo fatty acid biosynthesis. This is a 2 steps reaction starting with the ATP-dependent carboxylation of the biotin carried by the biotin carboxyl carrier (BCC) domain followed by the transfer of the carboxyl group from carboxylated biotin to acetyl-CoA.

gene.name: AKT serine/threonine kinase 1
gene.function: AKT1 is one of 3 closely related serine/threonine-protein kinases (AKT1, AKT2 and AKT3) called the AKT kinase, and which regulate many processes including metabolism, proliferation, cell survival, growth and angiogenesis. This is mediated through serine and/or threonine phosphorylation of a range of downstream substrates. Over 100 substrate candidates have been reported so far, but for most of them, no isoform specificity has been reported. AKT is responsible of the regulation of glucose uptake by mediating insulin-induced translocation of the SLC2A4/GLUT4 glucose transporter to the cell surface (By similarity). Phosphorylation of PTPN1 at 'Ser-50' negatively modulates its phosphatase activity preventing dephosphorylation of the insulin receptor and the attenuation of insulin signaling (By similarity). Phosphorylation of TBC1D4 triggers the binding of this effector to inhibitory 14-3-3 proteins, which is required for insulin-stimulated glucose transport. AKT also regulates the storage of glucose in the form of glycogen by phosphorylating GSK3A at 'Ser-21' and GSK3B at 'Ser-9', resulting in inhibition of its kinase activity (By similarity). Phosphorylation of GSK3 isoforms by AKT is also thought to be one mechanism by which cell proliferation is driven (By similarity). AKT also regulates cell survival via the phosphorylation of MAP3K5 (apoptosis signal-related kinase). Phosphorylation of 'Ser-83' decreases MAP3K5 kinase activity stimulated by oxidative stress and thereby prevents apoptosis. AKT mediates insulin-stimulated protein synthesis by phosphorylating TSC2 at 'Ser-939' and 'Thr-1462', thereby activating the mTORC1 signaling pathway, and leading to both phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 and in activation of RPS6KB1. Also regulates the mTORC1 signaling pathway by catalyzing phosphorylation of CASTOR1 and DEPDC5. AKT plays a role as key modulator of the AKT-mTOR signaling pathway controlling the tempo of the process of newborn neurons integration during adult neurogenesis, including correct neuron positioning, dendritic development and synapse formation (By similarity). Part of a positive feedback loop of mTORC2 signaling by mediating phosphorylation of MAPKAP1/SIN1, promoting mTORC2 activation (By similarity). AKT is involved in the phosphorylation of members of the FOXO factors (Forkhead family of transcription factors), leading to binding of 14-3-3 proteins and cytoplasmic localization. In particular, FOXO1 is phosphorylated at 'Thr-24', 'Ser-256' and 'Ser-319'. FOXO3 and FOXO4 are phosphorylated on equivalent sites. AKT has an important role in the regulation of NF-kappa-B-dependent gene transcription and positively regulates the activity of CREB1 (cyclic AMP (cAMP)-response element binding protein). The phosphorylation of CREB1 induces the binding of accessory proteins that are necessary for the transcription of pro-survival genes such as BCL2 and MCL1. AKT phosphorylates 'Ser-454' on ATP citrate lyase (ACLY), thereby potentially regulating ACLY activity and fatty acid synthesis (By similarity). Activates the 3B isoform of cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase (PDE3B) via phosphorylation of 'Ser-273', resulting in reduced cyclic AMP levels and inhibition of lipolysis (By similarity). Phosphorylates PIKFYVE on 'Ser-318', which results in increased PI(3)P-5 activity (By similarity). The Rho GTPase-activating protein DLC1 is another substrate and its phosphorylation is implicated in the regulation cell proliferation and cell growth (By similarity). Signals downstream of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI(3)K) to mediate the effects of various growth factors such as platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF), epidermal growth factor (EGF), insulin and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1). AKT mediates the antiapoptotic effects of IGF1 (By similarity). Essential for the SPATA13-mediated regulation of cell migration and adhesion assembly and disassembly. May be involved in the regulation of the placental development (By similarity). Phosphorylates STK4/MST1 at 'Thr-120' and 'Thr-387' leading to inhibition of its: kinase activity, nuclear translocation, autophosphorylation and ability to phosphorylate FOXO3. Phosphorylates STK3/MST2 at 'Thr-117' and 'Thr-384' leading to inhibition of its: cleavage, kinase activity, autophosphorylation at Thr-180, binding to RASSF1 and nuclear translocation. Phosphorylates SRPK2 and enhances its kinase activity towards SRSF2 and ACIN1 and promotes its nuclear translocation. Phosphorylates RAF1 at 'Ser-259' and negatively regulates its activity. Phosphorylation of BAD stimulates its pro-apoptotic activity. Phosphorylates KAT6A at 'Thr-369' and this phosphorylation inhibits the interaction of KAT6A with PML and negatively regulates its acetylation activity towards p53/TP53. Phosphorylates palladin (PALLD), modulating cytoskeletal organization and cell motility. Phosphorylates prohibitin (PHB), playing an important role in cell metabolism and proliferation. Phosphorylates CDKN1A, for which phosphorylation at 'Thr-145' induces its release from CDK2 and cytoplasmic relocalization. These recent findings indicate that the AKT1 isoform has a more specific role in cell motility and proliferation. Phosphorylates CLK2 thereby controlling cell survival to ionizing radiation. Phosphorylates PCK1 at 'Ser-90', reducing the binding affinity of PCK1 to oxaloacetate and changing PCK1 into an atypical protein kinase activity using GTP as donor. Also acts as an activator of TMEM175 potassium channel activity in response to growth factors: forms the lysoK(GF) complex together with TMEM175 and acts by promoting TMEM175 channel activation, independently of its protein kinase activity. Acts as a regulator of mitochondrial calcium uptake by mediating phosphorylation of MICU1 in the mitochondrial intermembrane space, impairing MICU1 maturation. Acts as an inhibitor of tRNA methylation by mediating phosphorylation of the N-terminus of METTL1, thereby inhibiting METTL1 methyltransferase activity. In response to LPAR1 receptor pathway activation, phosphorylates Rabin8/RAB3IP which alters its activity and phosphorylates WDR44 which induces WDR44 binding to Rab11, thereby switching Rab11 vesicular function from preciliary trafficking to endocytic recycling.

gene.name: arylsulfatase A
gene.function: Lysosomal enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of cerebroside-3-sulfate (N-acyl-1-beta-D-(3-O-sulfo)-galactosyl-sphing-4- enine) into cerebroside and sulfate, a reaction that requires the activator protein saposin B. Also involved in the catabolism of other sulfoglycosphingolipids such as SB1a and SM3 (beta-D-3-sulfogalactosyl- (1->4)-beta-D-glucosyl-(1<->1')-N-acylsphing-4-enine) (By similarity).

gene.name: autophagy related 7
gene.function: E1-like activating enzyme involved in the 2 ubiquitin-like systems required for cytoplasm to vacuole transport (Cvt) and autophagy. Activates ATG12 for its conjugation with ATG5 as well as the ATG8 family proteins for their conjugation with phosphatidylethanolamine. Both systems are needed for the ATG8 association to Cvt vesicles and autophagosomes membranes. Required for autophagic death induced by caspase-8 inhibition. Facilitates LC3-I lipidation with phosphatidylethanolamine to form LC3-II which is found on autophagosomal membranes. Required for mitophagy which contributes to regulate mitochondrial quantity and quality by eliminating the mitochondria to a basal level to fulfill cellular energy requirements and preventing excess ROS production. Modulates p53/TP53 activity to regulate cell cycle and survival during metabolic stress. Also plays a key role in the maintenance of axonal homeostasis, the prevention of axonal degeneration, the maintenance of hematopoietic stem cells, the formation of Paneth cell granules, as well as in adipose differentiation. Plays a role in regulating the liver clock and glucose metabolism by mediating the autophagic degradation of CRY1 (clock repressor) in a time-dependent manner (By similarity).

gene.name: CD1d molecule
gene.function: Antigen-presenting protein that binds self and non-self glycolipids and presents them to T-cell receptors on natural killer T- cells. .

gene.name: CLN3 lysosomal/endosomal transmembrane protein, battenin
gene.function: Mediates microtubule-dependent, anterograde transport connecting the Golgi network, endosomes, autophagosomes, lysosomes and plasma membrane, and participates in several cellular processes such as regulation of lysosomal pH, lysosome protein degradation, receptor- mediated endocytosis, autophagy, transport of proteins and lipids from the TGN, apoptosis and synaptic transmission. Facilitates the proteins transport from trans-Golgi network (TGN)-to other membrane compartments such as transport of microdomain-associated proteins to the plasma membrane, IGF2R transport to the lysosome where it regulates the CTSD release leading to regulation of CTSD maturation and thereby APP intracellular processing. Moreover regulates CTSD activity in response to osmotic stress. Also binds galactosylceramide and transports it from the trans Golgi to the rafts, which may have immediate and downstream effects on cell survival by modulating ceramide synthesis. At the plasma membrane, regulates actin-dependent events including filopodia formation, cell migration, and pinocytosis through ARF1-CDC42 pathway and also the cytoskeleton organization through interaction with MYH10 and fodrin leading to the regulation of the plasma membrane association of Na+, K+ ATPase complex. Regulates synaptic transmission in the amygdala, hippocampus, and cerebellum through regulation of synaptic vesicles density and their proximity to active zones leading to modulation of short-term plasticity and age-dependent anxious behavior, learning and memory (By similarity). Regulates autophagic vacuoles (AVs) maturation by modulating the trafficking between endocytic and autophagolysosomal/lysosomal compartments, which involves vesicle fusion leading to regulation of degradation process (By similarity). Also participates in cellular homeostasis of compounds such as, water, ions, amino acids, proteins and lipids in several tissue namely in brain and kidney through regulation of their transport and synthesis.

gene.name: cystinosin, lysosomal cystine transporter
gene.function: Cystine/H(+) symporter that mediates export of cystine, the oxidized dimer of cysteine, from lysosomes. Plays an important role in melanin synthesis by catalyzing cystine export from melanosomes, possibly by inhibiting pheomelanin synthesis. In addition to cystine export, also acts as a positive regulator of mTORC1 signaling in kidney proximal tubular cells, via interactions with components of the v-ATPase and Ragulator complexes. Also involved in small GTPase-regulated vesicle trafficking and lysosomal localization of LAMP2A, independently of cystine transporter activity (By similarity).

gene.name: cathepsin F
gene.function: Thiol protease which is believed to participate in intracellular degradation and turnover of proteins. Has also been implicated in tumor invasion and metastasis.

gene.name: alpha glucosidase
gene.function: Essential for the degradation of glycogen in lysosomes. Has highest activity on alpha-1,4-linked glycosidic linkages, but can also hydrolyze alpha-1,6-linked glucans.

gene.name: galactosylceramidase
gene.function: Hydrolyzes the galactose ester bonds of glycolipids such as galactosylceramide and galactosylsphingosine. Enzyme with very low activity responsible for the lysosomal catabolism of galactosylceramide, a major lipid in myelin, kidney and epithelial cells of small intestine and colon.

gene.name: galactosamine (N-acetyl)-6-sulfatase
gene.function: Lysosomal enzyme that hydrolyzes sulfate groups from glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), keratan sulfate (KS) and chondroitin-6- sulfate (C6S). .

gene.name: glucosylceramidase beta 1
gene.function: Glucosylceramidase that catalyzes, within the lysosomal compartment, the hydrolysis of glucosylceramides/GlcCers (such as beta- D-glucosyl-(1<->1')-N-acylsphing-4-enine) into free ceramides (such as N-acylsphing-4-enine) and glucose. Plays a central role in the degradation of complex lipids and the turnover of cellular membranes. Through the production of ceramides, participates in the PKC-activated salvage pathway of ceramide formation. Catalyzes the glucosylation of cholesterol, through a transglucosylation reaction where glucose is transferred from GlcCer to cholesterol. GlcCer containing mono-unsaturated fatty acids (such as beta-D- glucosyl-N-(9Z-octadecenoyl)-sphing-4-enine) are preferred as glucose donors for cholesterol glucosylation when compared with GlcCer containing same chain length of saturated fatty acids (such as beta-D- glucosyl-N-octadecanoyl-sphing-4-enine). Under specific conditions, may alternatively catalyze the reverse reaction, transferring glucose from cholesteryl 3-beta-D-glucoside to ceramide (Probable). Can also hydrolyze cholesteryl 3-beta-D- glucoside producing glucose and cholesterol. Catalyzes the hydrolysis of galactosylceramides/GalCers (such as beta-D-galactosyl-(1<->1')-N- acylsphing-4-enine), as well as the transfer of galactose between GalCers and cholesterol in vitro, but with lower activity than with GlcCers. Contrary to GlcCer and GalCer, xylosylceramide/XylCer (such as beta-D-xyosyl-(1<->1')-N-acylsphing-4- enine) is not a good substrate for hydrolysis, however it is a good xylose donor for transxylosylation activity to form cholesteryl 3-beta- D-xyloside. Can also metabolize plant glycosyl phytosterols such as glucosylstigmasterol.

gene.name: glucosylceramidase beta 2
gene.function: Non-lysosomal glucosylceramidase that catalyzes the hydrolysis of glucosylceramides/GlcCers (such as beta-D-glucosyl- (1<->1')-N-acylsphing-4-enine) to free glucose and ceramides (such as N-acylsphing-4-enine). GlcCers are membrane glycosphingolipids that have a wide intracellular distribution (By similarity). They are the main precursors of more complex glycosphingolipids that play a role in cellular growth, differentiation, adhesion, signaling, cytoskeletal dynamics and membrane properties (By similarity). Involved in the transglucosylation of cholesterol, transfers glucose from GlcCer to cholesterol, thereby modifying its water solubility and biological properties. Under specific conditions, may catalyze the reverse reaction, transferring glucose from cholesteryl-3-beta-D- glucoside to ceramide (such as N-acylsphing-4-enine) (Probable). May play a role in the metabolism of bile acids. Able to hydrolyze bile acid 3-O- glucosides as well as to produce bile acid-glucose conjugates thanks to a bile acid glucosyl transferase activity. Catalyzes the hydrolysis of galactosylceramides/GalCers (such as beta-D-galactosyl-(1<->1')-N- acylsphing-4-enine), as well as the galactosyl transfer between GalCers and cholesterol in vitro with lower activity compared with their activity against GlcCers.

gene.name: galactosidase alpha
gene.function: Catalyzes the hydrolysis of glycosphingolipids and participates in their degradation in the lysosome. .

gene.name: hexosaminidase subunit beta
gene.function: Hydrolyzes the non-reducing end N-acetyl-D-hexosamine and/or sulfated N-acetyl-D-hexosamine of glycoconjugates, such as the oligosaccharide moieties from proteins and neutral glycolipids, or from certain mucopolysaccharides. The isozyme B does not hydrolyze each of these substrates, however hydrolyzes efficiently neutral oligosaccharide. Only the isozyme A is responsible for the degradation of GM2 gangliosides in the presence of GM2A. During fertilization is responsible, at least in part, for the zona block to polyspermy. Present in the cortical granules of non-activated oocytes, is exocytosed during the cortical reaction in response to oocyte activation and inactivates the sperm galactosyltransferase-binding site, accounting for the block in sperm binding to the zona pellucida (By similarity).

gene.name: heat shock protein family A (Hsp70) member 2
gene.function: Molecular chaperone implicated in a wide variety of cellular processes, including protection of the proteome from stress, folding and transport of newly synthesized polypeptides, activation of proteolysis of misfolded proteins and the formation and dissociation of protein complexes. Plays a pivotal role in the protein quality control system, ensuring the correct folding of proteins, the re-folding of misfolded proteins and controlling the targeting of proteins for subsequent degradation. This is achieved through cycles of ATP binding, ATP hydrolysis and ADP release, mediated by co-chaperones. The affinity for polypeptides is regulated by its nucleotide bound state. In the ATP-bound form, it has a low affinity for substrate proteins. However, upon hydrolysis of the ATP to ADP, it undergoes a conformational change that increases its affinity for substrate proteins. It goes through repeated cycles of ATP hydrolysis and nucleotide exchange, which permits cycles of substrate binding and release. Plays a role in spermatogenesis. In association with SHCBP1L may participate in the maintenance of spindle integrity during meiosis in male germ cells (By similarity).

gene.name: heat shock protein family B (small) member 6
gene.function: Small heat shock protein which functions as a molecular chaperone probably maintaining denatured proteins in a folding- competent state. Seems to have versatile functions in various biological processes. Plays a role in regulating muscle function such as smooth muscle vasorelaxation and cardiac myocyte contractility. May regulate myocardial angiogenesis implicating KDR. Overexpression mediates cardioprotection and angiogenesis after induced damage. Stabilizes monomeric YWHAZ thereby supporting YWHAZ chaperone-like activity.

gene.name: alpha-L-iduronidase
gene.function: Lysosomal hydrolase responsible for the degradation of the glycosaminoglycans heparan sulfate and dermatan sulfate. .

gene.name: kinase insert domain receptor
gene.function: Tyrosine-protein kinase that acts as a cell-surface receptor for VEGFA, VEGFC and VEGFD. Plays an essential role in the regulation of angiogenesis, vascular development, vascular permeability, and embryonic hematopoiesis. Promotes proliferation, survival, migration and differentiation of endothelial cells. Promotes reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton. Isoforms lacking a transmembrane domain, such as isoform 2 and isoform 3, may function as decoy receptors for VEGFA, VEGFC and/or VEGFD. Isoform 2 plays an important role as negative regulator of VEGFA- and VEGFC-mediated lymphangiogenesis by limiting the amount of free VEGFA and/or VEGFC and preventing their binding to FLT4. Modulates FLT1 and FLT4 signaling by forming heterodimers. Binding of vascular growth factors to isoform 1 leads to the activation of several signaling cascades. Activation of PLCG1 leads to the production of the cellular signaling molecules diacylglycerol and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate and the activation of protein kinase C. Mediates activation of MAPK1/ERK2, MAPK3/ERK1 and the MAP kinase signaling pathway, as well as of the AKT1 signaling pathway. Mediates phosphorylation of PIK3R1, the regulatory subunit of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase, reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton and activation of PTK2/FAK1. Required for VEGFA-mediated induction of NOS2 and NOS3, leading to the production of the signaling molecule nitric oxide (NO) by endothelial cells. Phosphorylates PLCG1. Promotes phosphorylation of FYN, NCK1, NOS3, PIK3R1, PTK2/FAK1 and SRC.

gene.name: lysosomal protein transmembrane 4 alpha
gene.function: May function in the transport of nucleosides and/or nucleoside derivatives between the cytosol and the lumen of an intracellular membrane-bound compartment. .

gene.name: lysosomal protein transmembrane 4 beta
gene.function: Required for optimal lysosomal function. Blocks EGF-stimulated EGFR intraluminal sorting and degradation. Conversely by binding with the phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate, regulates its PIP5K1C interaction, inhibits HGS ubiquitination and relieves LAPTM4B inhibition of EGFR degradation. Recruits SLC3A2 and SLC7A5 (the Leu transporter) to the lysosome, promoting entry of leucine and other essential amino acid (EAA) into the lysosome, stimulating activation of proton-transporting vacuolar (V)-ATPase protein pump (V-ATPase) and hence mTORC1 activation. Plays a role as negative regulator of TGFB1 production in regulatory T cells. Binds ceramide and facilitates its exit from late endosome in order to control cell death pathways.

gene.name: mucolipin TRP cation channel 1
gene.function: Nonselective cation channel probably playing a role in the regulation of membrane trafficking events and of metal homeostasis. Acts as a Ca(2+)-permeable cation channel with inwardly rectifying activity. Proposed to play a major role in Ca(2+) release from late endosome and lysosome vesicles to the cytoplasm, which is important for many lysosome-dependent cellular events, including the fusion and trafficking of these organelles, exocytosis and autophagy. Required for efficient uptake of large particles in macrophages in which Ca(2+) release from the lysosomes triggers lysosomal exocytosis. May also play a role in phagosome-lysosome fusion (By similarity). Involved in lactosylceramide trafficking indicative for a role in the regulation of late endocytic membrane fusion/fission events. By mediating lysosomal Ca(2+) release is involved in regulation of mTORC1 signaling and in mTOR/TFEB-dependent lysosomal adaptation to environmental cues such as nutrient levels. Seems to act as lysosomal active oxygen species (ROS) sensor involved in ROS-induced TFEB activation and autophagy. Also functions as a Fe(2+) permeable channel in late endosomes and lysosomes. Also permeable to Mg(2+), Na(+), K(+) and Cs(+) (By similarity). Proposed to play a role in zinc homeostasis probably implicating its association with TMEM163 In adaptive immunity, TRPML2 and TRPML1 may play redundant roles in the function of the specialized lysosomes of B cells (By similarity).

gene.name: NPC intracellular cholesterol transporter 2
gene.function: Intracellular cholesterol transporter which acts in concert with NPC1 and plays an important role in the egress of cholesterol from the lysosomal compartment. Unesterified cholesterol that has been released from LDLs in the lumen of the late endosomes/lysosomes is transferred by NPC2 to the cholesterol-binding pocket in the N-terminal domain of NPC1. May bind and mobilize cholesterol that is associated with membranes. NPC2 binds cholesterol with a 1:1 stoichiometry. Can bind a variety of sterols, including lathosterol, desmosterol and the plant sterols stigmasterol and beta-sitosterol. The secreted form of NCP2 regulates biliary cholesterol secretion via stimulation of ABCG5/ABCG8-mediated cholesterol transport (By similarity).

gene.name: NPHS1 adhesion molecule, nephrin
gene.function: Seems to play a role in the development or function of the kidney glomerular filtration barrier. Regulates glomerular vascular permeability. May anchor the podocyte slit diaphragm to the actin cytoskeleton. Plays a role in skeletal muscle formation through regulation of myoblast fusion (By similarity). .

gene.name: phosphatase and tensin homolog
gene.function: Dual-specificity protein phosphatase, dephosphorylating tyrosine-, serine- and threonine-phosphorylated proteins. Also functions as a lipid phosphatase, removing the phosphate in the D3 position of the inositol ring of PtdIns(3,4,5)P3/phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5- trisphosphate, PtdIns(3,4)P2/phosphatidylinositol 3,4-diphosphate and PtdIns3P/phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate with a preference for PtdIns(3,4,5)P3. Furthermore, this enzyme can also act as a cytosolic inositol 3-phosphatase acting on Ins(1,3,4,5,6)P5/inositol 1,3,4,5,6 pentakisphosphate and possibly Ins(1,3,4,5)P4/1D-myo-inositol 1,3,4,5- tetrakisphosphate. Antagonizes the PI3K-AKT/PKB signaling pathway by dephosphorylating phosphoinositides and thereby modulating cell cycle progression and cell survival. The unphosphorylated form cooperates with MAGI2 to suppress AKT1 activation. In motile cells, suppresses the formation of lateral pseudopods and thereby promotes cell polarization and directed movement. Dephosphorylates tyrosine-phosphorylated focal adhesion kinase and inhibits cell migration and integrin-mediated cell spreading and focal adhesion formation. Required for growth factor-induced epithelial cell migration; growth factor stimulation induces PTEN phosphorylation which changes its binding preference from the p85 regulatory subunit of the PI3K kinase complex to DLC1 and results in translocation of the PTEN-DLC1 complex to the posterior of migrating cells to promote RHOA activation. Meanwhile, TNS3 switches binding preference from DLC1 to p85 and the TNS3-p85 complex translocates to the leading edge of migrating cells to activate RAC1 activation. Plays a role as a key modulator of the AKT-mTOR signaling pathway controlling the tempo of the process of newborn neurons integration during adult neurogenesis, including correct neuron positioning, dendritic development and synapse formation (By similarity). Involved in the regulation of synaptic function in excitatory hippocampal synapses. Recruited to the postsynaptic membrane upon NMDA receptor activation, is required for the modulation of synaptic activity during plasticity. Enhancement of lipid phosphatase activity is able to drive depression of AMPA receptor-mediated synaptic responses, activity required for NMDA receptor-dependent long-term depression (LTD) (By similarity). May be a negative regulator of insulin signaling and glucose metabolism in adipose tissue. The nuclear monoubiquitinated form possesses greater apoptotic potential, whereas the cytoplasmic nonubiquitinated form induces less tumor suppressive ability.

gene.name: RAB27A, member RAS oncogene family
gene.function: The small GTPases Rab are key regulators of intracellular membrane trafficking, from the formation of transport vesicles to their fusion with membranes. Rabs cycle between an inactive GDP-bound form and an active GTP-bound form that is able to recruit to membranes different sets of downstream effectors directly responsible for vesicle formation, movement, tethering and fusion. RAB27A regulates homeostasis of late endocytic pathway, including endosomal positioning, maturation and secretion. Plays a role in cytotoxic granule exocytosis in lymphocytes. Required for both granule maturation and granule docking and priming at the immunologic synapse.

gene.name: scavenger receptor class B member 2
gene.function: Acts as a lysosomal receptor for glucosylceramidase (GBA1) targeting. .

gene.name: synuclein alpha
gene.function: Neuronal protein that plays several roles in synaptic activity such as regulation of synaptic vesicle trafficking and subsequent neurotransmitter release. Participates as a monomer in synaptic vesicle exocytosis by enhancing vesicle priming, fusion and dilation of exocytotic fusion pores. Mechanistically, acts by increasing local Ca(2+) release from microdomains which is essential for the enhancement of ATP-induced exocytosis. Also acts as a molecular chaperone in its multimeric membrane-bound state, assisting in the folding of synaptic fusion components called SNAREs (Soluble NSF Attachment Protein REceptors) at presynaptic plasma membrane in conjunction with cysteine string protein-alpha/DNAJC5. This chaperone activity is important to sustain normal SNARE-complex assembly during aging. Also plays a role in the regulation of the dopamine neurotransmission by associating with the dopamine transporter (DAT1) and thereby modulating its activity.

gene.name: serine palmitoyltransferase small subunit A
gene.function: Component of the serine palmitoyltransferase multisubunit enzyme (SPT) that catalyzes the initial and rate-limiting step in sphingolipid biosynthesis by condensing L-serine and activated acyl-CoA (most commonly palmitoyl-CoA) to form long-chain bases. The SPT complex is composed of SPTLC1, SPTLC2 or SPTLC3 and SPTSSA or SPTSSB. Within this complex, the heterodimer consisting of SPTLC1 and SPTLC2/SPTLC3 forms the catalytic core. Within the SPT complex, SPTSSA stimulates the catalytic activity and plays a role in substrate specificity, which depends upon the overall complex composition. The SPTLC1-SPTLC2-SPTSSA complex shows a strong preference for C16-CoA substrate, while the SPTLC1-SPTLC3-SPTSSA isozyme uses both C14-CoA and C16-CoA as substrates, with a slight preference for C14-CoA. Independently of its action as a SPT component, may be involved in MBOAT7 localization to mitochondria-associated membranes, a membrane bridge between the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria, may hence affect MBOAT7- catalyzed incorporation of arachidonic acid into phosphatidylinositol.

gene.name: ST3 beta-galactoside alpha-2,3-sialyltransferase 5
gene.function: Transfers the sialyl group (N-acetyl-alpha-neuraminyl or NeuAc) from CMP-NeuAc to the non-reducing terminal galactose (Gal) of glycosphingolipids forming gangliosides (important molecules involved in the regulation of multiple cellular processes, including cell proliferation and differentiation, apoptosis, embryogenesis, development, and oncogenesis). Mainly involved in the biosynthesis of ganglioside GM3 but can also use different glycolipids as substrate acceptors such as D- galactosylceramide (GalCer), asialo-GM2 (GA2) and asialo-GM1 (GA1), although less preferentially than beta-D-Gal-(1->4)-beta-D-Glc-(1<->1)- Cer (LacCer).

gene.name: transcription factor EB
gene.function: Transcription factor that acts as a master regulator of lysosomal biogenesis, autophagy, lysosomal exocytosis, lipid catabolism, energy metabolism and immune response. Specifically recognizes and binds E-box sequences (5'-CANNTG-3'); efficient DNA-binding requires dimerization with itself or with another MiT/TFE family member such as TFE3 or MITF. Involved in the cellular response to amino acid availability by acting downstream of MTOR: in the presence of nutrients, TFEB phosphorylation by MTOR promotes its cytosolic retention and subsequent inactivation. Upon starvation or lysosomal stress, inhibition of MTOR induces TFEB dephosphorylation, resulting in nuclear localization and transcription factor activity. Specifically recognizes and binds the CLEAR-box sequence (5'-GTCACGTGAC-3') present in the regulatory region of many lysosomal genes, leading to activate their expression, thereby playing a central role in expression of lysosomal genes. Regulates lysosomal positioning in response to nutrient deprivation by promoting the expression of PIP4P1. Acts as a positive regulator of autophagy by promoting expression of genes involved in autophagy. In association with TFE3, activates the expression of CD40L in T-cells, thereby playing a role in T-cell-dependent antibody responses in activated CD4(+) T-cells and thymus-dependent humoral immunity (By similarity). Specifically recognizes the gamma-E3 box, a subset of E-boxes, present in the heavy- chain immunoglobulin enhancer. Plays a role in the signal transduction processes required for normal vascularization of the placenta (By similarity). Involved in the immune response to infection by the bacteria S.aureus, S.typhimurium or S.enterica: infection promotes itaconate production, leading to alkylation, resulting in nuclear localization and transcription factor activity. Itaconate-mediated alkylation activates TFEB- dependent lysosomal biogenesis, facilitating the bacteria clearance during the antibacterial innate immune response. In association with ACSS2, promotes the expression of genes involved in lysosome biogenesis and both autophagy upon glucose deprivation.

gene.name: transmembrane protein 165
gene.function: Putative divalent cation:proton antiporter that exchanges calcium or manganese ions for protons across the Golgi membrane. Mediates the reversible transport of calcium or manganese to the Golgi lumen driven by the proton gradient and possibly the membrane potential generated by V-ATPase. Provides calcium or manganese cofactors to resident Golgi enzymes and contributes to the maintenance of an acidic luminal Golgi pH required for proper functioning of the secretory pathway (By similarity). Promotes Ca(2+) storage within the Golgi lumen of the mammary epithelial cells to be then secreted into milk (By similarity). The transport mechanism and stoichiometry remains to be elucidated.

gene.name: tripartite motif containing 27
gene.function: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that mediates ubiquitination of various substrates and thereby plays a role in diffent processes including proliferation, innate immunity, apoptosis, immune response or autophagy. Ubiquitinates PIK3C2B and inhibits its activity by mediating the formation of 'Lys-48'-linked polyubiquitin chains; the function inhibits CD4 T-cell activation. Acts as a regulator of retrograde transport: together with MAGEL2, mediates the formation of 'Lys-63'-linked polyubiquitin chains at 'Lys-220' of WASHC1, leading to promote endosomal F-actin assembly. Has a transcriptional repressor activity by cooperating with EPC1. Induces apoptosis by activating Jun N-terminal kinase and p38 kinase and also increases caspase-3-like activity independently of mitochondrial events. May function in male germ cell development. Has DNA-binding activity and preferentially bound to double-stranded DNA. Forms a complex with and ubiquitinates the ubiquitin-specific protease USP7, which in turn deubiquitinates RIPK1 resulting in the positive regulation of TNF-induced apoptosis. In addition, acts with USP7 or PTPN11 as an inhibitor of the antiviral signaling pathway by promoting kinase TBK1 ubiquitination and degradation. Acts as a negative regulator of NOD2 signaling by mediating ubiquitination of NOD2, promoting its degradation by the proteasome. Alternatively, facilitates mitophagy via stabilization of active TBK1. Negatively regulates autophagy flux under basal conditions by directly polyubiquitinating ULK1. During starvation-induced autophagy, catalyzes non-degradative ubiquitination of the kinase STK38L promoting its activation and phosphorylation of ULK1 leading to its ubiquitination and degradation to restrain the amplitude and duration of autophagy.

gene.name: transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily V member 1
gene.function: Non-selective calcium permeant cation channel involved in detection of noxious chemical and thermal stimuli. Seems to mediate proton influx and may be involved in intracellular acidosis in nociceptive neurons. Involved in mediation of inflammatory pain and hyperalgesia. Sensitized by a phosphatidylinositol second messenger system activated by receptor tyrosine kinases, which involves PKC isozymes and PCL. Activated by vanilloids, like capsaicin, and temperatures higher than 42 degrees Celsius. Upon activation, exhibits a time- and Ca(2+)-dependent outward rectification, followed by a long-lasting refractory state. Mild extracellular acidic pH (6.5) potentiates channel activation by noxious heat and vanilloids, whereas acidic conditions (pH <6) directly activate the channel. Can be activated by endogenous compounds, including 12-hydroperoxytetraenoic acid and bradykinin. Acts as ionotropic endocannabinoid receptor with central neuromodulatory effects. Triggers a form of long-term depression (TRPV1-LTD) mediated by the endocannabinoid anandamine in the hippocampus and nucleus accumbens by affecting AMPA receptors endocytosis.

papers.title: Oral pharmacological chaperone migalastat compared with enzyme replacement therapy in Fabry disease: 18-month results from the randomised phase III ATTRACT study.
papers.summary: The 18-month ATTRACT study found that oral migalastat maintained renal function, plasma lyso-Gb3, patient-reported outcomes, and safety comparably to intravenous enzyme replacement therapy in previously treated adults with Fabry disease and amenable GLA mutations. Migalastat was associated with a significant reduction in left ventricular mass index, while non-amenable mutations showed increased plasma lyso-Gb3 after switching from ERT.
papers.why: The randomized ATTRACT trial provides direct comparative clinical evidence for oral migalastat versus intravenous enzyme replacement therapy in amenable Fabry mutations.

papers.title: Treatment of Fabry disease: outcome of a comparative trial with agalsidase alfa or beta at a dose of 0.2 mg/kg.
papers.summary: In a randomized open-label comparison of agalsidase alfa and agalsidase beta at 0.2 mg/kg every two weeks, both preparations reduced plasma and urinary globotriaosylceramide but produced similar, generally nonsignificant effects on left ventricular mass, renal function, pain, and treatment-failure rates. Treatment failure was frequent and associated with older age, greater pre-treatment severity, and advanced renal dysfunction, indicating limited efficacy in severely affected patients.
papers.why: This comparative clinical trial directly tests two approved enzyme-replacement products in Fabry disease and reports treatment outcomes and failure measures.

papers.title: Ten-year outcome of enzyme replacement therapy with agalsidase beta in patients with Fabry disease.
papers.summary: In a 10-year follow-up of 52 patients with classic Fabry disease receiving intravenous agalsidase beta, 81% remained free of severe clinical events and 94% were alive; plasma globotriaosylceramide normalized within 6 months. Outcomes were most favorable in younger patients with less pre-existing renal involvement, while renal function continued to decline in both low- and high-involvement groups and cardiac wall thickness progressed in patients aged 40 years or older at treatment initiation.
papers.why: Ten-year clinical trial and registry follow-up provide direct outcome data for agalsidase beta in Fabry disease and identify treatment-response determinants.

papers.title: Head-to-head trial of pegunigalsidase alfa versus agalsidase beta in patients with Fabry disease and deteriorating renal function: results from the 2-year randomised phase III BALANCE study.
papers.summary: In adults with Fabry disease and deteriorating renal function who had prior agalsidase beta exposure, 2 years of pegunigalsidase alfa was non-inferior to agalsidase beta for annualised estimated glomerular filtration rate slope. Pegunigalsidase alfa produced substantially fewer infusion-related reactions and treatment-emergent adverse events, although serious hypersensitivity and immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis occurred in individual patients.
papers.why: The randomized BALANCE trial provides two-year comparative evidence establishing pegunigalsidase alfa as noninferior to agalsidase beta for renal outcomes.

papers.title: Characterization of small fiber pathology in a mouse model of Fabry disease.
papers.summary: In GLA knockout mice, age-dependent Gb3 accumulation in dorsal root ganglion neurons is associated with endoplasmic stress, apoptosis, reduced skin innervation, altered TRPV1 protein expression, and reduced Ih and Nav1.7 currents. In a GLA-silenced HEK293 cell model, agalsidase-α and lucerastat reversed Gb3 deposits and restored Nav1.7 currents, supporting a direct functional effect of intracellular Gb3 on neuronal ion channels.
papers.why: The paper characterizes a disease-specific small-fiber model and demonstrates reversal of Gb3 accumulation and Nav1.7-current loss by agalsidase alfa and lucerastat.

papers.title: Fabry Disease: Current and Novel Therapeutic Strategies. A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review concludes that Fabry disease can be managed with approved enzyme-replacement and chaperone therapies that stabilize disease manifestations, while substrate-reduction and gene therapies remain investigational. Diagnostic biomarkers and organ-specific supportive care are important, but available disease-specific therapies have limitations involving eligibility, infusions, antibodies, and limited central nervous system exposure.
papers.why: The review summarizes multiple clinically available or experimentally tested Fabry therapies, including chaperone, enzyme replacement, substrate reduction, and gene-therapy approaches.

papers.title: Phase 1 Healthy Volunteer Study of AL01211, an Oral, Non-brain Penetrant Glucosylceramide Synthase Inhibitor, to Treat Fabry Disease and Type 1 Gaucher Disease.
papers.summary: The Phase 1 healthy-volunteer study found that oral glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor AL01211 was generally well tolerated and reduced plasma glucosylceramide and globotriacylceramide in an exposure-dependent manner. The findings support further development for Fabry disease and Type 1 Gaucher disease, but the trial did not enroll patients with either disease.
papers.why: Reports a phase 1 study of an oral substrate-reduction drug developed for Fabry disease, including pharmacokinetics, safety, and dose-related reduction of plasma globotriaosylceramide.

papers.title: Dapagliflozin in Patients With CKD With Fabry Disease.
papers.summary: In a 16-patient prospective cohort with Fabry disease and albuminuric chronic kidney disease, add-on dapagliflozin was associated with lower 24-hour proteinuria and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio, while eGFR remained stable during 12 months of treatment. The preliminary findings suggest renal stabilization beyond stable enzyme replacement therapy or migalastat plus renin-angiotensin system inhibition, but causal interpretation is limited by the uncontrolled, small, heterogeneous cohort and short follow-up.
papers.why: This prospective multicenter Fabry study provides direct evidence that dapagliflozin reduces albuminuria/proteinuria and slows renal decline in patients already receiving disease-specific therapy.

papers.title: Epigenetic Modifiers as Potential Therapeutic Targets in Diabetic Kidney Disease.
papers.summary: The paper identifies apabetalone as an epigenetic modifier being evaluated in a planned phase 1/2 trial that includes patients with Fabry disease. It states that Fabry disease is caused by GLA mutations, produces glycolipid accumulation with kidney and heart disease, and shares pathogenic pathways with diabetic kidney disease, but it reports no efficacy or safety results from the Fabry trial.
papers.why: Apabetalone and SGLT2 inhibition are clinically tested strategies relevant to the kidney disease and cardiac-renal protection phenotypes of Fabry disease.

papers.title: Fabry disease: progression of nephropathy, and prevalence of cardiac and cerebrovascular events before enzyme replacement therapy.
papers.summary: This retrospective multicenter study characterizes the pre-ERT natural history of Fabry disease in 447 patients, finding faster and more advanced nephropathy in males than females and associations of proteinuria, reduced baseline eGFR, hypertension, and male sex with progression. Cardiac events, especially arrhythmias, and cerebrovascular events were common, while the paper discusses recombinant agalsidase alfa and agalsidase beta as enzyme replacement therapies reported in prior studies to stabilize renal function and clear GL-3.
papers.why: The study provides quantitative Fabry nephropathy progression measures and clinically associated predictors that can serve as biomarkers and trial outcomes.

papers.title: Recommendations for initiation and cessation of enzyme replacement therapy in patients with Fabry disease: the European Fabry Working Group consensus document.
papers.summary: This European consensus paper recommends when to initiate or stop enzyme replacement therapy in patients with a definite diagnosis of Fabry disease, distinguishing classical from non-classical disease and males from females. The recommendations are based mainly on expert opinion, observational studies, and limited randomized evidence, while reported evidence suggests potential reductions in cardiac mass and renal Gb3 accumulation but less certain effects on nervous-system disease and renal function.
papers.why: This consensus document provides actionable disease-specific criteria for selecting Fabry patients for ERT and for discontinuing treatment.

papers.title: Long-term outcome of enzyme-replacement therapy in advanced Fabry disease: evidence for disease progression towards serious complications.
papers.summary: In a prospective 6-year observational cohort, enzyme-replacement therapy with agalsidase beta improved neuropathic pain and hypohidrosis in many patients with advanced Fabry disease but did not prevent myocardial fibrosis, ventricular tachycardia, sudden cardiac death, stroke, end-stage renal disease, or decline in glomerular filtration rate. The composite event rate did not differ significantly from a matched untreated natural-history cohort, although the nonrandomized design, small sample, and advanced age of participants limit causal conclusions.
papers.why: Prospective six-year Fabry study directly evaluates ERT against major clinical and organ-disease outcomes.

papers.title: The validation of pharmacogenetics for the identification of Fabry patients to be treated with migalastat.
papers.summary: The paper clinically validates a GLP HEK/Migalastat Amenability Assay that expresses individual GLA mutant forms in HEK-293 cells and identifies Fabry patients whose mutant α-galactosidase A responds to migalastat. Assay classifications agreed with patient pharmacodynamic responses, and migalastat reduced kidney GL-3 inclusions or plasma lyso-Gb3 in patients with amenable mutations, whereas nonamenable patients did not show consistent reductions.
papers.why: The paper validates a GLP laboratory assay that identifies Fabry mutations amenable to migalastat and predicts biochemical treatment response.

papers.title: Reproducibility of native myocardial T1 mapping in the assessment of Fabry disease and its role in early detection of cardiac involvement by cardiovascular magnetic resonance.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 63 genotyped patients with Fabry disease, CMR-derived native myocardial T1 mapping was highly reproducible and identified reduced myocardial T1 before left ventricular hypertrophy. Among patients without hypertrophy, low native T1 was associated with impaired systolic and diastolic cardiac function, supporting its potential for early cardiac-involvement detection.
papers.why: The study demonstrates that native T1 mapping is reproducible in Fabry disease and detects early myocardial involvement before left ventricular hypertrophy.

papers.title: Functional characterisation of alpha-galactosidase a mutations as a basis for a new classification system in fabry disease.
papers.summary: The study shows that an in vitro HEK293H overexpression system using residual alpha-galactosidase A activity can classify the clinical severity of 171 GLA mutations more accurately than plasma lyso-Gb3 or PolyPhen2 predictions. DGJ restored enzyme levels or activity for many mutants, particularly class II mutants, but most active-site substitutions and only 14.5% of class I mutants could not be rescued, while lyso-Gb3 was less reliable in mildly affected females.
papers.why: The paper develops a Fabry-specific functional mutation-testing framework and tests a pharmacological chaperone as a mutation-analysis tool.

papers.title: Migalastat: A Review in Fabry Disease.
papers.summary: This review concludes that oral migalastat stabilizes amenable mutant α-galactosidase A, increases its lysosomal activity, reduces glycosphingolipid substrates, and improves or preserves selected renal, gastrointestinal, and cardiac outcomes in patients with Fabry disease carrying migalastat-amenable GLA mutations. Benefits are mutation-dependent, while the primary FACETS endpoint was not significantly different in the overall intent-to-treat population, and evidence for severe clinical events, pregnancy, childhood, and severe renal impairment remains limited.
papers.why: This review summarizes controlled trial evidence for migalastat effects on substrate biomarkers, kidney inclusions, renal function, cardiac mass, and tolerability.

papers.title: The New York pilot newborn screening program for lysosomal storage diseases: Report of the First 65,000 Infants.
papers.summary: The New York pilot newborn-screening program screened 65,605 infants for Fabry disease using dried-blood-spot α-galactosidase A activity, followed by confirmatory enzyme, DNA, and biomarker testing where applicable. It detected 31 screen-positive infants, including seven true positives predicted to have type 2 late-onset Fabry disease; the c.239G>A (p.G80D) variant was interpreted as likely benign, and no infants were receiving disease-specific treatment at the time of the report.
papers.why: Provides large-scale newborn-screening data that include Fabry disease and demonstrate feasibility of confirmatory testing and follow-up.

papers.title: Pilot study of newborn screening for six lysosomal storage diseases using Tandem Mass Spectrometry.
papers.summary: The pilot study showed that a six-plex flow injection-MS/MS newborn-screening assay can measure α-galactosidase A activity in dried blood spots and identify newborns at risk for Fabry disease. Among approximately 43,000 newborns, 8 GLA screen-positive samples were genotyped: three were classified as affected, with p.K213N or p.R356Q variants, while two had normal GLA sequences and two had benign variants.
papers.why: Reports a multiplex newborn-screening assay that directly measures GLA activity and confirms Fabry disease risk genetically.

papers.title: Fabry disease: identification of 50 novel alpha-galactosidase A mutations causing the classic phenotype and three-dimensional structural analysis of 29 missense mutations.
papers.summary: The study identified 50 novel GLA mutations in 66 unrelated families with classic Fabry disease, substantially expanding the molecular spectrum of disease-causing variants. Structural modelling and transient expression in COS-7 cells distinguished mutations associated with active-site disruption, protein misfolding or ER retention, and highlighted several structurally tolerated variants that nevertheless caused severe functional loss and therefore may merit pharmacological-chaperone studies.
papers.why: The paper identifies causal GLA variants and experimentally and structurally characterizes their functional effects, providing directly reusable diagnostic and modeling methods.

papers.title: Time to treatment benefit for adult patients with Fabry disease receiving agalsidase β: data from the Fabry Registry.
papers.summary: In an uncontrolled analysis of 1044 adults with Fabry disease receiving agalsidase β, severe clinical events declined after the first 6 months of treatment and remained at 40–58 events per 1000 patient-years, with the largest absolute reductions in older and male patients. The paper associates this approximately 6-month lag to clinical benefit with the previously reported clearance of GL-3 deposits from vascular endothelial cells, but registry selection bias, absent untreated controls, and incomplete follow-up prevent a definitive causal conclusion.
papers.why: Uses registry data from 1,044 treated adults to show reduced severe renal, cardiac, cerebrovascular, and mortality events after approximately six months of agalsidase beta.

papers.title: Agalsidase alfa versus agalsidase beta for the treatment of Fabry disease: an international cohort study.
papers.summary: In a 387-patient international retrospective cohort, agalsidase alfa and agalsidase beta produced similar clinical event rates and eGFR slopes at their registered doses, although agalsidase beta produced greater reductions in plasma lysoGb3 and left ventricular mass index and more persisting antibodies. The stronger biochemical response to agalsidase beta was observed even among antibody-positive men, but biochemical superiority was not accompanied by a detectable difference in clinical events.
papers.why: The international cohort study directly compares two registered enzyme replacement therapies using clinical, renal, cardiac, antibody, and LysoGb3 outcomes.

papers.title: Phenotypic characteristics of the p.Asn215Ser (p.N215S) GLA mutation in male and female patients with Fabry disease: A multicenter Fabry Registry study.
papers.summary: A multicenter Fabry Registry natural-history study of 125 patients with the GLA p.N215S variant found severe manifestations primarily involving the heart, with progressive ventricular-wall thickening and frequent cardiac events, especially in males. Renal and cerebrovascular manifestations were uncommon, although late renal impairment occurred in a minority, and the authors proposed that loss of the N-linked glycan at residue 215 alters α-galactosidase A folding and lysosomal trafficking.
papers.why: This multicenter Fabry Registry study provides mutation-specific natural-history data and validated cardiac, renal, and cerebrovascular outcome measures for the p.N215S variant.

papers.title: Effectiveness of agalsidase alfa enzyme replacement in Fabry disease: cardiac outcomes after 10 years' treatment.
papers.summary: In a retrospective 10-year cohort study, continuous agalsidase alfa enzyme replacement therapy was associated with improved or stable heart failure and angina classifications, attenuation of left ventricular hypertrophy, and generally preserved cardiac and renal function in adults with Fabry disease. Urinary protein increased in men with pre-existing proteinuria, and the absence of a untreated control group limits causal conclusions.
papers.why: A 10-year Fabry cohort shows clinical and echocardiographic benefits of agalsidase alfa, including improved heart-failure class and stabilized left-ventricular hypertrophy.

papers.title: Efficacy of the pharmacologic chaperone migalastat in a subset of male patients with the classic phenotype of Fabry disease and migalastat-amenable variants: data from the phase 3 randomized, multicenter, double-blind clinical trial and extension study.
papers.summary: In a post hoc subset analysis of the phase 3 FACETS trial, oral migalastat increased peripheral blood mononuclear cell α-galactosidase A activity and reduced cardiac mass, diarrhea symptoms, renal globotriaosylceramide inclusions, and plasma globotriaosylsphingosine in men with classic Fabry disease and migalastat-amenable GLA variants. eGFR was reported as stabilized, but the classic-phenotype sample was small, follow-up was limited to 24 months, and no formal statistical testing was performed.
papers.why: The FACETS trial analysis provides clinical outcome and biomarker data supporting migalastat efficacy in male patients with classic Fabry disease and amenable variants.

papers.title: Elevated Inflammatory Plasma Biomarkers in Patients With Fabry Disease: A Critical Link to Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
papers.summary: In a multicenter observational cohort of 68 patients with Fabry disease, multiple inflammatory, extracellular-matrix remodeling, natriuretic-peptide, and lysoglycosphingolipid biomarkers were elevated relative to healthy controls and were associated with cardiac hypertrophy, fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction, renal dysfunction, or greater disease burden. Plasma Lyso-Gb3 was highly diagnostic of classic Fabry disease, but its diagnostic performance was poor for cardiac/renal variants, while observational associations involving enzyme replacement therapy could not establish treatment benefit or harm.
papers.why: Multicenter Fabry data show that inflammatory, cardiac-remodeling, renal, and glycosphingolipid biomarkers correlate with hypertrophy, diastolic dysfunction, fibrosis, renal disease, and progression.

papers.title: Mutations in the GLA Gene and LysoGb3: Is It Really Anderson-Fabry Disease?
papers.summary: In approximately 17,000 people evaluated for Fabry-related symptoms, the study found concordant GLA variants, deficient α-galactosidase A activity, and blood LysoGb3 accumulation in patients with classic or late-onset Fabry disease. The authors propose combining clinical history, GLA analysis, α-galactosidase A assay, and LysoGb3 measurement to distinguish pathogenic Fabry disease from variants of unknown significance and noncausal intronic variants.
papers.why: The study validates LysoGb3 and a combined biochemical-genetic diagnostic strategy in a large Fabry disease cohort.

papers.title: Safety and pharmacodynamic effects of a pharmacological chaperone on α-galactosidase A activity and globotriaosylceramide clearance in Fabry disease: report from two phase 2 clinical studies.
papers.summary: In two combined open-label phase 2 studies, orally administered migalastat increased α-galactosidase A activity and reduced globotriaosylceramide in blood, urine, skin, or kidney in 6 of 9 men with Fabry disease whose missense GLA mutations were amenable in a HEK-293 cell assay. Migalastat was well tolerated, but the uncontrolled studies were small, heterogeneous, and insufficient to establish long-term clinical efficacy.
papers.why: Two Phase 2 studies show that migalastat increases alpha-Gal A activity and reduces GL-3 in patients with responsive GLA variants, with an in vitro assay predicting responsiveness.

papers.title: Challenging the traditional approach for interpreting genetic variants: Lessons from Fabry disease.
papers.summary: This review and case-based expert analysis shows that Fabry disease diagnosis requires integration of GLA variant classification with α-galactosidase A activity, plasma or urinary lyso-Gb3 measurements, family segregation, and expert clinical judgment. It identifies p.(Ala143Thr), p.(Asp313Tyr), p.(Ser126Gly), p.(Arg118Cys), and p.(Glu66Gln) as likely benign or benign bystanders, while emphasizing the limitations of prediction software, generic population-frequency thresholds, amenability tables, and isolated clinical findings.
papers.why: The study shows that expert clinical, phenotype, inheritance, biomarker, and population-frequency analysis improves interpretation of uncertain and pathogenic GLA variants.

papers.title: Effectiveness of plasma lyso-Gb3 as a biomarker for selecting high-risk patients with Fabry disease from multispecialty clinics for genetic analysis.
papers.summary: The prospective multicenter study found that elevated plasma globotriaosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb3), measured by ultra-performance liquid chromatography/tandem mass spectrometry, identified previously unrecognized male and female probands with classic or late-onset Fabry disease. Plasma α-galactosidase A activity alone was less reliable in females, and normal lyso-Gb3 could not reliably exclude Fabry disease in women, children, or patients with late-onset disease.
papers.why: Clinical screening data support plasma lyso-Gb3 as a primary biomarker for identifying classic and late-onset Fabry disease probands.

papers.title: Enzyme replacement therapy for Anderson-Fabry disease: A complementary overview of a Cochrane publication through a linear regression and a pooled analysis of proportions from cohort studies.
papers.summary: This systematic review and pooled analysis of 77 cohort studies involving 15,305 participants found that agalsidase beta was associated with lower incidence of renal, cardiovascular, and cerebrovascular complications than no enzyme replacement therapy, and with fewer cerebrovascular events than agalsidase alfa. Mortality and adverse-event rates did not differ significantly among treatment groups, but substantial heterogeneity and limited long-term individual-patient data limit the strength of the comparisons.
papers.why: This large systematic review and pooled cohort analysis directly evaluates established Fabry enzyme-replacement therapies and clinically important outcomes.

papers.title: Oral Chaperone Therapy Migalastat for Treating Fabry Disease: Enzymatic Response and Serum Biomarker Changes After 1 Year.
papers.summary: In a prospective 14-patient follow-up, one year of oral migalastat increased alpha-galactosidase A activity and was associated with a modest reduction in myocardial mass, while cardiac biomarkers remained stable. Globotriaosylsphingosine declined in therapy-naive patients but was not consistently stabilized after switching from enzyme replacement therapy, and estimated glomerular filtration rate declined significantly.
papers.why: The prospective one-year study provides real-world evidence that migalastat increases alpha-Gal A activity, reduces myocardial mass, and changes lyso-Gb3 and renal measures in amenable Fabry disease.

papers.title: A pharmacogenetic approach to identify mutant forms of α-galactosidase A that respond to a pharmacological chaperone for Fabry disease.
papers.summary: The study shows that AT1001 (migalastat hydrochloride) increased activity and protein levels of many mutant α-Gal A forms in a HEK-293 cell assay, with responses observed for 49 of 81 variants tested. The assay responses correlated with responses in male Fabry patient lymphoblasts and PBMCs after oral AT1001, supporting its use as a complementary pharmacogenetic aid for identifying potentially responsive variants, although clinical benefit was not established.
papers.why: The study develops and validates a cell-based assay that identifies GLA variants likely to respond to migalastat using clinically achievable drug concentrations.

papers.title: Co-administration with the pharmacological chaperone AT1001 increases recombinant human α-galactosidase A tissue uptake and improves substrate reduction in Fabry mice.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the pharmacological chaperone AT1001 (migalastat) stabilizes recombinant human α-galactosidase A, prolongs its circulation, and increases its cellular and tissue uptake, thereby enhancing GL-3 reduction in Fabry patient-derived fibroblasts and GLA knockout mice. These preclinical findings support further clinical investigation of AT1001 as a coadministration strategy with α-galactosidase A enzyme replacement therapy, but do not establish clinical efficacy in patients.
papers.why: In vitro, rat, and Fabry-mouse experiments show that migalastat stabilizes recombinant alpha-Gal A and substantially improves its half-life, tissue uptake, and GL-3 reduction.

papers.title: Use of a rare disease registry for establishing phenotypic classification of previously unassigned GLA variants: a consensus classification system by a multispecialty Fabry disease genotype-phenotype workgroup.
papers.summary: A five-stage expert consensus method combining Fabry Registry clinical data, a hallmark-symptom 2-point score, and severe-event-free survival validation assigned pathogenic classic or later-onset phenotypes to 32 of 33 previously unclassified GLA variants. The classifications reproduced the earlier and later onset of severe clinical events in males and generally extended to females, while p.Ala143Thr remained of uncertain significance and several classifications disagreed with database or in silico results.
papers.why: The workgroup develops and clinically validates a consensus system for assigning phenotypes and clinical risk to previously unclassified GLA variants.

papers.title: Immune-Mediated Myocarditis in Fabry Disease Cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 78 patients with Fabry disease cardiomyopathy, histological myocarditis was frequent, increased in prevalence with left ventricular hypertrophy, and was associated with CD3+ T-cell infiltration, myocyte necrosis, antiheart/antimyosin autoantibodies, but no detectable cardiotropic viral genome. The authors interpret the inflammation as immune-mediated and potentially contributory to disease progression and enzyme replacement therapy resistance, while cardiac magnetic resonance detects only a subset of histologically evident cases.
papers.why: The study validates histological, serologic, and MRI approaches for detecting immune-mediated myocarditis in Fabry cardiomyopathy.

papers.title: Acid hydrolases in leukocytes and platelets of normal subjects and in patients with Gaucher's and Fabry's disease.
papers.summary: In a small comparative study, blood cells from one patient with Fabry disease showed deficient alpha-galactosidase activity while all other tested acid hydrolases had normal activity. Blood cells from three patients with Gaucher disease showed pH 4.0 acid beta-glucosidase deficiency, variable pH 5.0 beta-glucosidase activity, and normal activity for the remaining tested hydrolases.
papers.why: The study directly demonstrates deficient alpha-galactosidase activity in blood cells from a patient with Fabry disease.

papers.title: LC-MS/MS multiplex analysis of lysosphingolipids in plasma and amniotic fluid: A novel tool for the screening of sphingolipidoses and Niemann-Pick type C disease.
papers.summary: The paper developed and clinically validated a multiplex LC-MS/MS assay for plasma lysosphingolipids, with lysoglobotriaosylceramide (LysoGb3) elevated in all tested patients with Fabry disease. LysoGb3 measurement showed 100% sensitivity in the Fabry cohort, including females and late-onset variants, but the paper requires diagnostic confirmation by appropriate enzymatic or genetic analysis and notes that slight nonspecific elevations can occur in other disorders.
papers.why: The study developed and clinically validated a multiplex LC-MS/MS assay that sensitively and specifically screens for Fabry disease using plasma lysoglobotriaosylceramide.

papers.title: A Human Stem Cell Model of Fabry Disease Implicates LIMP-2 Accumulation in Cardiomyocyte Pathology.
papers.summary: Patient-derived GLA-mutant iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes modeled Fabry disease and exhibited GL-3 accumulation, increased electrical excitability, altered calcium handling, and a distinct proteomic and secretomic profile. Genetic correction reversed the principal biomarker changes, while LIMP-2 overexpression induced cathepsin F and HSP70-2 secretion and extensive vacuole formation, implicating LIMP-2 accumulation in cardiomyocyte pathology.
papers.why: The gene-edited iPSC cardiomyocyte model reproduces Fabry cardiac phenotypes and identifies candidate biomarkers whose changes are reversed by genetic correction.

papers.title: Implementation of Second-Tier Tests in Newborn Screening for Lysosomal Disorders in North Eastern Italy.
papers.summary: In a North Eastern Italian newborn-screening cohort, multiplexed enzyme screening followed by confirmatory testing identified eight newborns with late-onset Fabry disease. Reduced GLA activity and pathogenic GLA variants supported diagnosis, but LysoGb3 was only slightly elevated in five patients measured in plasma and normal in most patients measured in dried blood spots, limiting its value as a neonatal second-tier test.
papers.why: Large-scale newborn screening data show that MS/MS plus second-tier testing can rapidly identify Fabry disease while reducing false positives.

papers.title: Switch from enzyme replacement therapy to oral chaperone migalastat for treating fabry disease: real-life data.
papers.summary: In a seven-man observational cohort with migalastat-amenable GLA variants, switching from agalsidase alfa or beta enzyme replacement therapy to migalastat maintained most renal, cardiac, neurologic, pain, and health-status measures for 12 months while increasing α-galactosidase A activity and reducing plasma lyso-Gb3. Left ventricular mass index and proteinuria improved modestly, and adverse-event frequency was comparable between treatments, but the single-center cohort was small and follow-up was short.
papers.why: Real-world longitudinal data support switching amenable Fabry patients from ERT to migalastat, showing acceptable safety and improvements or stability across cardiac, renal, pain, and biomarker outcomes.

papers.title: Antiproteinuric therapy and Fabry nephropathy: factors associated with preserved kidney function during agalsidase-beta therapy.
papers.summary: In a 21-month prospective observational study of 24 adults with classical Fabry nephropathy receiving agalsidase-beta, antiproteinuric treatment with ACE inhibitors and/or angiotensin II receptor blockers allowed 18 patients to reach the prespecified urine protein to creatinine ratio goal. Proteinuria control was associated with slower eGFR decline, but only six of the 18 goal-achieving patients had preserved kidney function; younger age at agalsidase-beta initiation was the only significant predictor of preservation, and hypotension and hyperkalaemia required treatment modification.
papers.why: This Fabry nephropathy study reports outcomes from agalsidase beta combined with antiproteinuric ACE inhibitor or ARB treatment and identifies a proteinuria target associated with better kidney-function preservation.

papers.title: Human kidney organoids reveal the role of glutathione in Fabry disease.
papers.summary: The paper establishes CRISPR/Cas9-generated GLA-knockout human iPSC kidney organoids as an in vitro model of renal Fabry disease, reproducing Gb3 accumulation, zebra bodies, cellular deformation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis. Recombinant human α-Gal A improved several abnormalities but did not eliminate them, while glutathione replacement restored redox measures, improved organoid structure and renal-cell marker expression, and reduced apoptosis.
papers.why: This study develops a patient-relevant GLA-mutant kidney organoid model and demonstrates rescue of Gb3 accumulation, oxidative stress, and structural abnormalities by enzyme replacement or glutathione.

papers.title: Oral Migalastat HCl Leads to Greater Systemic Exposure and Tissue Levels of Active α-Galactosidase A in Fabry Patients when Co-Administered with Infused Agalsidase.
papers.summary: In 23 adult men with Fabry disease, single-dose migalastat hydrochloride co-administered with agalsidase alfa or beta increased systemic exposure to active α-galactosidase A and generally increased enzyme activity in skin and peripheral blood mononuclear cells compared with agalsidase alone. The interaction was not clearly dose-dependent, agalsidase did not measurably alter migalastat exposure, and the small single-dose study did not establish clinical benefit or support formal statistical conclusions for skin and PBMC activity.
papers.why: The Phase 2a trial found that adding migalastat to agalsidase increased active alpha-Gal A exposure in plasma, skin, and PBMCs in 22 of 23 Fabry patients.

papers.title: Newborn screening for Fabry disease in the north-west of Spain.
papers.summary: The study found one newborn with a classic Fabry disease-associated GLA variant, estimated a male prevalence of 0.013%, and showed that a fluorometric α-galactosidase A assay followed by GLA sequencing had high overall accuracy but a low positive predictive value and a substantial false-positive rate. The findings support systematic newborn screening but show that frequent variants of uncertain significance and the p.D313Y pseudodeficiency allele complicate interpretation and management.
papers.why: The study demonstrates a feasible population newborn-screening workflow for Fabry disease and identifies the need to characterize variants of uncertain significance.

papers.title: Newborn Screening for Fabry Disease in Northeastern Italy: Results of Five Years of Experience.
papers.summary: A 5.5-year newborn-screening program in northeastern Italy used dried-blood-spot α-galactosidase A activity followed by biochemical and GLA molecular testing to identify 22 males with reduced enzyme activity and GLA variants, most associated with later-onset Fabry disease. Plasma lyso-Gb3 was useful for longitudinal biochemical monitoring and, when clearly elevated at birth, could simplify referral, but a normal dried-blood-spot lyso-Gb3 result did not exclude Fabry disease and was therefore unreliable as a second-tier screening test.
papers.why: Large-scale newborn screening data demonstrate a multiplex assay workflow for early Fabry detection and indicate when lyso-Gb3 testing is useful for follow-up monitoring.

papers.title: Pharmacological chaperone therapy for Fabry disease.
papers.journal: Proc Jpn Acad Ser B Phys Biol Sci
papers.summary: This review reports that 1-deoxygalactonojirimycin (DGJ) acts as a pharmacological chaperone for mutant α-galactosidase A, facilitating proper folding, lysosomal trafficking, and enzymatic activity while reducing globotriaosylceramide accumulation. Effects were demonstrated in mutant-enzyme expression systems, patient-derived cells, and an R301Q transgenic/knockout mouse model, with phase 2 findings summarized as increased α-Gal A and reduced globotriaosylceramide, but therapy is limited to Fabry variants whose mechanism includes protein misfolding.
papers.why: The study demonstrates that 1-deoxygalactonojirimycin stabilizes and traffics mutant alpha-galactosidase A, increasing organ activity and reducing globotriaosylceramide in a Fabry mouse model.

papers.title: Generation of GLA-Knockout Human Embryonic Stem Cell Lines to Model Autophagic Dysfunction and Exosome Secretion in Fabry Disease-Associated Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: This study generated CRISPR/Cas9-edited GLA-knockout human embryonic stem cell lines and differentiated them into cardiomyocytes that accumulated Gb3, enlarged, and expressed cardiac hypertrophy markers, thereby modeling Fabry disease-associated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. In these cells, GLA knockout was associated with reduced Rab GTPase-related vesicle-trafficking proteins, impaired autophagic flux, increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, and increased apoptosis and necrosis.
papers.why: The paper creates and validates a human GLA-null stem-cell-derived cardiomyocyte model exhibiting Gb3 accumulation and hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy phenotypes.

papers.title: Accumulation of α-synuclein mediates podocyte injury in Fabry nephropathy.
papers.summary: Human kidney biopsies and a CRISPR/Cas9 GLA-knockout podocyte model show that enzyme replacement therapy with agalsidase beta reduces globotriaosylceramide inclusions but does not fully reverse podocyte injury or lysosomal dysfunction. α-Synuclein accumulation mediates part of the Gb3-independent lysosomal phenotype, and genetic reduction or β2-adrenergic receptor agonism improves lysosomal measures in cultured Fabry podocytes, although β2-agonists may be unsafe in patients prone to arrhythmias.
papers.why: The Fabry podocyte experiments identify alpha-synuclein accumulation as an injury mechanism and show that genetic or pharmacological alpha-synuclein inhibition improves lysosomal function beyond enzyme replacement therapy.

papers.title: Possible role of transforming growth factor-β1 and vascular endothelial             growth factor in Fabry disease nephropathy.
papers.summary: In an α-galactosidase A-knockout Fabry mouse model, renal TGF-β1, VEGF, VEGFR2, FGF-2, phosphorylated p38, and selected caspase signals were elevated, supporting a possible apoptotic mechanism for Fabry nephropathy. Gb3-treated bovine aortic endothelial cells reproduced the growth-factor and signaling changes, while Fabrazyme treatment reduced renal caspase-3/7 activity relative to untreated Fabry mice; however, caspase-3/7 activity was not significantly different between Fabry and wild-type mice, and apoptotic changes had not been demonstrated in renal biopsies from Fabry patients.
papers.why: The study uses Fabry mouse kidneys and Gb3-exposed endothelial cells to identify mechanistic markers associated with nephropathy and apoptosis.

papers.title: Glucosylceramide synthase inhibition with lucerastat lowers globotriaosylceramide and lysosome staining in cultured fibroblasts from Fabry patients with different mutation types.
papers.summary: In cultured fibroblasts from 15 Fabry patients carrying 13 pathogenic GLA variants, lucerastat dose-dependently reduced globotriaosylceramide, globotriaosylsphingosine in some lines, and LysoTracker staining, including in cells with negligible residual α-galactosidase A activity. Agalsidase alfa also reduced the markers in many lines, whereas migalastat produced no consistent dose-responsive effects, although the in vitro findings require clinical validation.
papers.why: Lucerastat dose-dependently reduced Gb3 accumulation and lysosomal staining across 15 Fabry patient fibroblast lines carrying diverse GLA mutations.

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy Study of Several Replagal Dosing Regimens on Cardiac Function in Adults With Fabry Disease
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to compare the safety and effectiveness of various doses of Replagal in patients with cardiomyopathy due to Fabry disease.

papers.title: An Open-Label Clinical Trial of Replagal Enzyme Therapy in Children Ages 7-17 Years With Fabry Disease
papers.summary:
This study will evaluate the safety of multiple biweekly intravenous doses of Replagal over 26 weeks in 25 children with Fabry disease and the way in which that agent can improve the health of this patient population. Fabry disease is a genetic disorder inherited as an X-linked recessive trait. It causes a deficiency in the enzyme alpha galactosidase, which normally breaks down a lipid, or fatty substance, called ceramidetrihexosidase, a building block in all cells of the body.

Fabrazyme is a drug that helps to breakdown and remove certain types of fatty substances called "glycolipids." These glycolipids are normally present within the body in most cells.
