papers.title: Open Label Extension of 2 mg/kg Pegunigalsidase Alfa (PRX-102) Every 4 Weeks in Adult Fabry Disease Patients
papers.summary: The objective of CLI-06657AA1-03 (formerly PB-102-F51) is to evaluate the long-term safety, tolerability, and efficacy of 2 mg/kg pegunigalsidase alfa administered intravenously every four weeks in adult Fabry patients who have successfully completed PB-102-F50.

papers.title: Alpha-Galactosidase A Replacement Therapy for Fabry Disease
papers.summary: This study will determine the safety of the drug Replagal or treating patients with Fabry disease, an inherited metabolic disorder. In this disease, an enzyme called Alpha-galactosidase A, which normally breaks down a fatty substance called globotriaosylceramide (Gb3), is missing or does not function properly. The resulting accumulation of Gb3 causes problems with the kidneys, heart, nerves, and blood vessels. Replagal is a genetically engineered form of Alpha-galactosidase A. papers.title: A Study to Evaluate the Effect of Venglustat Tablets on Neuropathic and Abdominal Pain in Male and Female Participants ≥16 Years of Age With Fabry Disease
papers.summary:
This is a 12-month, parallel treatment, Phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the effect of venglustat on neuropathic and abdominal pain symptoms of Fabry disease in participants ≥16 years of age with Fabry disease who are treatment-naïve or untreated for at least 6 months.

* Study visits will take place approximately every 3 months.
* The double-blind period will be followed by an open-label extension (OLE) during which participants who have completed the double-blind period will be treated with venglustat for an additional 12 months or until the Common Stud

papers.title: A Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Fabrazyme in Patients With Fabry Disease
papers.summary: People with Fabry disease have an alteration in their genetic material (DNA) which causes a deficiency of the alpha-galactosidase A enzyme. This enzyme helps to break down and remove certain types of fatty substances called "glycolipids." These glycolipids are normally present within the body in most cells. papers.title: Study of the Safety and Efficacy of PRX-102 Compared to Agalsidase Beta on Renal Function
papers.summary: This was a randomized, double-blind, active control study of the enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) drug PRX-102 (pegunigalsidase alfa) in Fabry disease patients with impaired renal function. Patients who had been treated for approximately 1 year with agalsidase beta and who had been on a stable dose of that product for at least 6 months were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to either switch to PRX-102 or to continue treatment with agalsidase beta. Both treatments were delivered by intravenous infusions every two weeks, at a dosage of 1 mg/kg.

papers.title: Safety Study of Replagal® Therapy in Children With Fabry Disease
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to assess the safety of Replagal in children with Fabry disease who who have not previously been treated with enzyme replacement therapy (ERT).

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy of PRX-102 in Patients With Fabry Disease Currently Treated With REPLAGAL® (Agalsidase Alfa)
papers.summary: This is an open label switch over study to assess the safety and efficacy of PRX-102 (pegunigalsidase alfa). Patients treated with agalsidase alfa for at least 2 years and on a stable dose (\>80% labelled dose/kg) for at least 6 months. Patients will be screened and evaluated over 3 months while continuing on agalsidase alfa. Following the screening period, the patient will be enrolled and switched from their agalsidase alfa treatment to receive intravenous (IV) infusions of PRX-102 1 mg/kg every two weeks for 12 months. No more than 25% of treated patients will be female.

* To assess the effect of Replagal on heart rate variability in patients 7 to 17 years of age

Secondary Objective(s):

* To determine the pharmacokinetics of Replagal at baseline and after the initiation of enzyme replacement therapy (ERT)

papers.title: A Fabry Disease Gene Therapy Study
papers.summary: This is a multinational, open-label study to assess the safety and efficacy of FLT190 in up to 15 adult male participants with classical Fabry disease.

papers.title: Evaluate the Safety and Exploratory Efficacy of GC1119
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and exploratory efficacy of GC1119 (recombinant human α-galactosidase A) for enzyme replacement therapy in Fabry disease patients.

papers.title: Prevalence of Fabry's Disease in a Population of Patients With Chronic Pains
papers.summary: Fabry disease (FD) is a rare X-linked multisytemic lysosomal disorder caused by alpha-galactosidase deficiency. Globotriaosylcéramide (Gb3) deposits are observed in almost all tissues examined. Signs of the disease appear earlier and are more severe in affected males than in females. Myocardiopathy, renal failure and neurological signs including chronic pain and peripheral neuropathies are the most frequent signs. The availability of two enzymatic replacement therapies now provides a specific and effective treatment for patients. The prevalence of FD is estimated between 1/40,000 and 1/117,000

papers.title: Study to Evaluate the Safety and EffIcacy of PRX-102 on Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Naïve Fabry Disease
papers.summary: The study will be a randomized, double blind, placebo-controlled study of the safety and efficacy of PRX-102 in ERT naïve male patients randomized 1:1. Patient age will be 14 to 45 years. Patients must have diarrhea defined as ≥ 3 stools a day with an average consistency of ≥ 5.5 on the Bristol Stool Form Scale (BSFS) by patient electronic diary and moderate to severe gastrointestinal symptoms as defined by the Irritable Bowel Symptom Severity Score (IBSSS) Part 1 average \> 175 derived from at least two IBSSS assessments during screening period. papers.title: A Safety and Efficacy Study of Fabrazyme® Replacement Therapy in Patients With Cardiac Fabry Disease
papers.summary:
This is a multi-center, open label, phase IV study conducted to evaluate the efficacy and safety of agalsidase beta (Fabrazyme \[recombinant form\]) administered by intravenous drip infusion in participants with cardiac Fabry disease.

Participants participated for 4 weeks or less in the baseline period and 156 weeks for the treatment period.

papers.title: Evaluation of the Gastrointestinal Manifestation of Fabry's Disease
papers.summary: Patients will undergo a SmartPill test to gain additional understanding of Fabry disease manifestation via motility abnormalities in order to improve symptom targeted therapy. An additional Endoscopic mucosal resection may be performed on further qualifying patients. Tissue analysis from this biopsy will include evaluation of abnormalities of cellular structure and morphology with correlation with gastrointestinal complaints for each patient and comparison against age matched non-Fabry patient tissue. The hypothesis is that patients with fabry disease will have abnormal motility which will cor

papers.title: A Long Term Follow-Up Study of Fabry Disease Subjects Treated With FLT190
papers.summary: Fabry disease is a rare, X-linked inborn error of glycosphingolipid metabolism caused by an abnormal gene encoding the α-galactosidase A (αGLA) enzyme. The αGLA enzyme is ubiquitously expressed throughout the body and is responsible for the breakdown of glycosphingolipids, deficiency of which results in the accumulation of specific glycosphingolipids that are associated with the pathophysiology of the disease. Current treatment for Fabry disease is limited to the symptomatic management of pain, conventional management of complications, and methods to increase the availability of functional αGL

papers.title: China Post-marketing Surveillance (PMS) Study of Fabrazyme®
papers.summary: This is a 54-week Phase 4, open label, single arm study to evaluate the safety and the efficacy of Fabrazyme (agalsidase beta) as enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) in Chinese participants with Fabry Disease.

papers.title: The Safety and Efficacy of Intravenous EXG110 in Patients With Fabry Disease
papers.summary: A phase 1/2, multicenter, open-label, Dose-escalation study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of intravenous EXG110 in patients with Fabry disease

papers.title: An Open-label, Phase 1/2 Trial of Gene Therapy 4D-310 in Adults With Fabry Disease
papers.summary: This is a prospective multicenter, open-label, dose-escalation trial to assess the safety, tolerability, and pharmacodynamics of 4D-310 following a single IV administration. The study population is comprised of adult males and females with Fabry Disease.

papers.title: Safety, Pharmacodynamics, and Efficacy of Migalastat in Pediatric Subjects (Aged >12 Years) With Fabry Disease
papers.summary: This is a long-term, Open-label Study to Evaluate the Safety, Pharmacodynamics, and Efficacy of Migalastat in Subjects \> 12 Years of Age With Fabry Disease and Amenable GLA Variants

papers.title: Migalastat Food Effect Study
papers.summary: A 5-period crossover study to evaluate the effect of meal type and timing on migalastat HCl pharmacokinetics in healthy male and female subjects. Subjects will be randomly assigned to 1 of 5 treatment sequences and will receive each treatment over the course of 5 weekly periods.

papers.title: Dose-Ranging Study of ST-920, an AAV2/6 Human Alpha Galactosidase A Gene Therapy in Subjects With Fabry Disease (STAAR)
papers.summary: This is the first in human treatment with ST-920, an adeno-associated virus (AAV2/6) vector encoding the complementary deoxyribonucleic acid (cDNA) for human a-Gal A. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of ascending doses of ST-920. ST-920 aims to provide stable, long-term production of α-Gal A at therapeutic levels in subjects with Fabry disease. The constant production of α-Gal A in humans should, importantly, enable reduction and potentially clearance of Fabry disease substrates Gb3 and lyso-Gb3. On Day 1, patients will be infused intravenously with a single

papers.title: Alternative Dosing and Regimen of Replagal to Treat Fabry Disease
papers.summary:
The main goal of this study is to assess the pharmacodynamic effects of different or more frequent doses of Replagal compared to the standard dosing regimen. Replagal is a genetically engineered form of alpha-Galactosidase A, an enzyme that normally breaks down a fatty substance called globotriaosylceramide (Gb(3)). In patients with Fabry disease, GB(3) does not function properly and therefore builds up causing problems with the kidneys, heart, nerves, and blood vessels.

Male patients 18 years of age or older with Fabry disease who are not on dialysis and have not received a kidney transplant

papers.title: Dosing Study of Replagal in Patients With Fabry Disease
papers.summary:
This study will determine the safety and effectiveness of increasing Replagal infusions in certain patients with Fabry disease. Replagal is a genetically engineered form of Alpha-galactosidase A, an enzyme that normally breaks down a fatty substance called globotriaosylceramide (Gb3). In patients with Fabry disease, Alpha-galactosidase A does not function properly and, therefore, Gb3 builds up, causing problems with the kidneys, heart, nerves, and blood vessels.

Patients with Fabry disease who are participating in NIH protocol 00-N-0185 or 02-N-0220 may be eligible for this study. This includ

papers.title: Evaluation of the Long-term Safety, Pharmacodynamics, and Exploratory Efficacy of GZ/SAR402671 in Treatment-Naïve Adult Male Patients With Fabry Disease
papers.summary:
Primary Objective:

To assess the long-term safety of GZ/SAR402671 in adult male participants with Fabry disease who previously completed study ACT13739 (NCT02489344).

Secondary Objective:

To assess the long-term effect of GZ/SAR402671 on pharmacodynamic and exploratory efficacy endpoints in adult male participants with Fabry disease who previously completed study ACT13739.

papers.title: A Study of Replagal in Children and Adults With Fabry Disease in India
papers.summary:
The main aim of this study is to learn more about the safety profile of Replagal.

Participants will receive Replagal every 2 weeks at the clinic for about 1 year.

papers.title: A Study to Assess the Safety and Tolerability of Lucerastat in Subjects With Fabry Disease
papers.summary:
The primary purpose of this study was to assess the safety and tolerability of lucerastat in adults with Fabry Disease receiving Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT).

The secondary objectives were to investigate the effects of lucerastat on plasma and urine levels of biomarkers, to assess its effects on renal and cardiac functions and to determine the pharmacokinetic profile of lucerastat at steady-state.

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy of Gabapentin for Neuropathic Pain in Fabry Disease
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine efficacy of gabapentin vs. placebo at controlling peripheral neuropathic pain in patients with Fabry disease, and reducing their use of opioid analgesics. The investigators are conducting a randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled, single center, cross-over study. The primary endpoint is percent reduction in patients' use of hydrocodone-acetaminophen.

papers.title: Severe Renal Disease Study in Fabry Patients Treated With Fabrazyme
papers.summary: This study was designed to determine appropriate treatment with Fabrazyme at a biweekly dose of either 1 mg/kg or 3 mg/kg in a population of patients with severe renal disease burden.

papers.title: A Study to Evaluate Migalastat in Fabry Subjects With Amenable GLA Variant and Renal Disease
papers.summary: An Open-label Study to Evaluate the Safety and Pharmacokinetics of Migalastat HCl in Subjects with Fabry Disease and Amenable GLA Variants and Severe Renal Impairment (SRI) or End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD)

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for Fabry disease
Open Targets drugs acting on GLA
Peripheral neuropathy in metachromatic leukodystrophy: current status and future perspective.
papers.summary: This review reports that metachromatic leukodystrophy (MLD) is caused by deficient lysosomal arylsulfatase A (ASA/ARSA) activity, leading to sulfatide accumulation, demyelination, and peripheral neuropathy. Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation corrects ASA deficiency but has limited peripheral effects, while hematopoietic stem cell gene therapy produced stable or improved nerve conduction in some patients; intravenous enzyme replacement therapy has not shown clinical benefit for the central or peripheral nervous system, and AAV-based gene therapy failed in one trial.

papers.title: Chaperone therapy for neuronopathic lysosomal diseases: competitive inhibitors as chemical chaperones for enhancement of mutant enzyme activities.
papers.summary: This review reports that pharmacologic chaperones can restore catalytic activity from unstable mutant lysosomal enzymes by stabilizing folding and transport to the lysosome. For the transferable mechanism α-galactosidase A activity, galactose and 1-deoxygalactonojirimycin (DGJ) increased activity in Fabry disease cells, although galactose required an unrealistic high concentration; analogous valienamine derivatives produced mutation-dependent rescue and neurological benefit in β-galactosidase and β-glucosidase disease models.

papers.title: Azasugar inhibitors as pharmacological chaperones for Krabbe disease.
papers.summary: This paper primarily characterizes galacto-configured azasugars as pharmacological chaperone candidates for GALC in Krabbe disease, finding that IGF and AGF bind the GALC active site and increase its thermal stability through a charge-mediated interaction with E258. For transfer to Fabry disease, the paper specifically identifies 1-deoxy-galacto-nojirimycin as an α-galactosidase A stabilizer undergoing phase III Fabry disease trials, although that Fabry evidence is cited rather than newly reported here.

papers.title: Hemorrhagic aspects of Gaucher disease.
papers.summary: This review describes Gaucher disease as a lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient glucocerebrosidase activity, with Gaucher-cell infiltration and abnormalities of platelet number and function, coagulation factors, and fibrinolysis. It reports that enzyme replacement therapy improves hematologic manifestations and partially corrects coagulopathies, but it provides no evidence concerning α-galactosidase A activity or Fabry disease.

papers.title: Enzyme-Loaded Gel Core Nanostructured Lipid Carriers to Improve Treatment of Lysosomal Storage Diseases: Formulation and In Vitro Cellular Studies of Elosulfase Alfa-Loaded Systems.
papers.summary: This paper shows that PEGylated, elosulfase alfa-loaded nanostructured lipid carriers can preserve enzyme activity, enter human chondrocytes and MPS IVA patient fibroblasts, release functional GALNS in lysosomes, reduce glycosaminoglycan accumulation, and distribute to multiple tissues in mice. It provides a transferable lysosomal-enzyme delivery platform, but contains no direct experiments on Fabry disease, GLA, or α-galactosidase A activity.

papers.title: Residual glycosaminoglycan accumulation in mitral and aortic valves of a patient with attenuated MPS I (Scheie syndrome) after 6 years of enzyme replacement therapy: Implications for early diagnosis and therapy.
papers.summary: This case report shows that 6 years of enzyme replacement therapy reduced systemic urinary glycosaminoglycan levels but did not prevent progression of established aortic and mitral valve disease in attenuated mucopolysaccharidosis type I. It provides no evidence about α-galactosidase A activity or a treatment acting on that Fabry disease mechanism.

papers.title: Genetics and Therapies for GM2 Gangliosidosis.
papers.summary: This review describes GM2 gangliosidosis, in which impaired GM2 ganglioside degradation causes lysosomal storage and neurodegeneration, and evaluates enzymatic, substrate-reduction, chaperone, and gene-transfer strategies. It reports promising rAAV gene-transfer rescue in Sandhoff mice, cats, and sheep, but limited or absent clinical benefit for several other approaches; the paper does not describe globotriaosylceramide or a Fabry-specific treatment acting on that mechanism.

papers.title: A CRISPR Screen Identifies LAPTM4A and TM9SF Proteins as Glycolipid-Regulating Factors.
papers.summary: A genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screen identified LAPTM4A and TM9SF2 as post-transcriptional regulators of globotriaosylceramide synthesis in HeLa cells. Loss of either protein reduced globotriaosylceramide, with LAPTM4A regulating Gb3 synthase activity and TM9SF2 maintaining its Golgi/trans-Golgi-network localization.

papers.title: Iminosugar-based inhibitors of glucosylceramide synthase increase brain glycosphingolipids and survival in a mouse model of Sandhoff disease.
papers.summary: In Sandhoff disease mice, the blood-brain barrier-permeant glucosylceramide synthase inhibitors Genz-529468 and NB-DNJ improved motor function, reduced brain histopathology, and extended survival, but paradoxically increased rather than decreased brain glycosphingolipids. The paper therefore reports that these benefits may arise from off-target anti-inflammatory or lipid-profile effects rather than CNS substrate reduction, and it cites substrate reduction therapy as potentially applicable to Fabry disease without testing it in that disease.

papers.title: Repurposing of tamoxifen ameliorates CLN3 and CLN7 disease phenotype.
papers.summary: The paper identifies lysosomal globotriaosylceramide accumulation in CLN3 and CLN7 Batten disease models and develops a Shiga-toxin-based cell-based imaging assay that also detects globotriaosylceramide accumulation in a GLA-knockout model of Fabry disease. Tamoxifen clears globotriaosylceramide in Batten disease cells and mice through TFEB activation, but the study does not report tamoxifen efficacy in the Fabry disease model.

papers.title: Neurological deficits and glycosphingolipid accumulation in saposin B deficient mice.
papers.summary: Saposin B-deficient knock-in mice accumulated globotriaosylceramide (TriCer/Gb3) and lactosylceramide in multiple tissues, supporting saposin B’s role in their degradation, particularly through assistance of α-galactosidase A. The mice also developed neurological dysfunction, storage inclusions, and neuroinflammation, providing a model for studying glycosphingolipid metabolism and saposin–enzyme interactions relevant to globotriaosylceramide biology.

papers.title: TRPML1 activation ameliorates lysosomal phenotypes in CLN3 deficient retinal pigment epithelial cells.
papers.summary: In CLN3-knockout ARPE-19 retinal pigment epithelial cells, the TRPML1 agonist ML-SA5 reduced lysosomal accumulation of globotriaosylceramide, mitochondrial ATPase subunit C, and glycerophosphodiesters. The globotriaosylceramide reduction was TFEB-independent, whereas depleted bis(monoacylglycerol)phosphates were not restored, and efficacy in Fabry disease or in vivo was not tested.

papers.title: Targeting oxidative stress-induced lipid peroxidation enhances podocyte function in cystinosis.
papers.summary: In cystinosis, CTNS loss causes mitochondrial dysfunction, increased mitochondrial superoxide, lipid peroxidation, ferroptosis, podocyte detachment, and increased glomerular permeability. MitoTEMPO and liproxstatin-1 improve podocyte adhesion and barrier function in patient-derived and CTNS-knockdown podocytes, and rescue proteinuria in a cystinosis zebrafish larval model.

papers.title: Enhanced Levels of Glycosphingolipid GM3 Delay the Progression of Diabetic Nephropathy.
papers.summary: Valproic acid-induced enhancement of podocyte GM3 expression protected podocytes and reduced albuminuria, serum creatinine, glomerular lesions, and mesangial expansion in mice with streptozotocin-induced diabetic nephropathy. Human kidney biopsies showed that reduced podocyte GM3 and nephrin expression correlated with increased proteinuria, supporting GM3 as a podocyte-protection mechanism that may warrant testing in podocyte-mediated proteinuric diseases.

papers.title: Glycosphingolipid GM3 prevents albuminuria and podocytopathy induced by anti-nephrin antibody.
papers.summary: Valproic acid prevented anti-nephrin-antibody-induced podocytopathy in wild-type mice and nephrin-injury cells by increasing ST3GAL5-dependent GM3, which stabilized nephrin and retained slit-diaphragm and membrane-raft integrity. The protective effect was absent in St3gal5−/− mice, showing that GM3 is required for this podocyte-protective mechanism in the studied models.

papers.title: Progression of albuminuria and podocyte injury in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis inhibited by enhanced glycosphingolipid GM3 via valproic acid.
papers.summary: In anti-nephrin antibody-induced mouse models, valproic acid increased GM3 expression and attenuated established albuminuria, glomerulosclerosis, podocyte loss, foot-process effacement, and loss of nephrin and integrin β1. The protective effect was absent in St3gal5−/− mice, supporting an essential role for GM3 in podocyte function.

papers.title: TRIM27-controlled endothelium-derived exosomes play a central role in podocyte injury in diabetic kidney disease.
papers.summary: The paper shows that glomerular endothelial-cell exosomes carrying miR-486-5p injure podocytes in diabetic kidney disease through the PTEN/Akt pathway, with TRIM27 promoting exosome production by activating STAT3 and increasing Rab27a. Endothelial-cell TRIM27 or miR-486-5p knockdown, exosome-secretion inhibition, miR-486-5p inhibition, PTEN overexpression, and Akt inhibition reduced podocyte injury or proteinuria in cultured cells and diabetic mice.

papers.title: Elevated Prorenin Induces Podocyte Injury and Glomerular Fibrosis in cyp1a1-Prorenin Transgenic Rats.
papers.summary: In cyp1a1-prorenin transgenic rats, inducible elevation of circulating prorenin caused podocyte loss, foot-process effacement, albuminuria, and glomerular fibrosis independently of hyperglycemia. Amlodipine and enalapril prevented hypertension and partially rescued podocyte injury and fibrosis, with suppression of NF-κB- and Nox2-associated inflammatory and oxidative signaling, but neither treatment fully normalized the kidney defects.

papers.title: Trehalose reduces retinal degeneration, neuroinflammation and storage burden caused by a lysosomal hydrolase deficiency.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of mucopolysaccharidosis IIIB caused by NAGLU deficiency, oral trehalose increased survival, improved behavior, preserved retinal structure and function, reduced neuroinflammation, and decreased autophagic-vacuole storage burden. Molecular analyses showed increased autophagic flux and activation of the TFEB autophagy-lysosomal transcriptional network, supporting transfer of this mechanism to lysosomal storage diseases such as Fabry disease, although no Fabry-specific experiments were performed.

papers.title: Modeling CNS Involvement in Pompe Disease Using Neural Stem Cells Generated from Patient-Derived Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells.
papers.summary: Pompe disease patient-derived iPSC neural stem cells reproduced glycogen accumulation, enlarged lysosomes, and secondary lipid accumulation associated with lysosomal storage. Recombinant human GAA partially rescued lysosomal enlargement and glycogen accumulation, while δ-tocopherol plus hydroxypropyl-beta-cyclodextrin reduced multiple storage-related phenotypes, with limitations from the small, mutation-homogeneous cell panel and in vitro design.

papers.title: Characterization of Drosophila Saposin-related mutants as a model for lysosomal sphingolipid storage diseases.
papers.summary: The paper establishes Drosophila Sap-r2.2 null mutants as an animal model of sphingolipid-related lysosomal storage disease, with lipid accumulation, enlarged endo-/lysosomal compartments, impaired autophagic flux, oxidative stress, reduced viability, and progressive neurodegeneration. Sap-r re-expression rescues the enlarged endo-/lysosomal phenotype, while LysoTracker, lipid-profiling, microscopy, and behavioral assays provide tools for studying this storage mechanism and its downstream consequences.

papers.title: Liver-Directed Human Amniotic Epithelial Cell Transplantation Improves Systemic Disease Phenotype in Hurler Syndrome Mouse Model.
papers.summary: In an Idua knockout mouse model of Hurler syndrome, liver-directed transplantation of human amniotic epithelial cells restored hepatic IDUA activity, reduced urinary glycosaminoglycan excretion, and improved skeletal and sensorimotor phenotypes. The study provides a preclinical lysosomal enzyme-replacement strategy for MPS1, a lysosomal storage disorder, although tissue-wide IDUA restoration and skeletal changes were incomplete.

papers.title: Lentiviral gene therapy prevents anti-human acid α-glucosidase antibody formation in murine Pompe disease.
papers.summary: In an immunocompetent Gaa−/− mouse model of Pompe disease, subtherapeutic HSPC-mediated lentiviral GAA gene therapy induced immune tolerance to both the transgene product and subsequent recombinant human GAA enzyme replacement therapy. Gene therapy followed by 100 mg/kg weekly ERT prevented anti-rhGAA antibody formation and ERT-associated death, while ERT normalized muscle glycogen levels and rotarod performance; this supports a possible strategy for preventing anti-enzyme antibodies in lysosomal storage disorders.

papers.title: Deficiency in NPC2 results in disruption of mitochondria-late endosome/lysosomes contact sites and endo-lysosomal lipid dyshomeostasis.
papers.summary: NPC2-knockout HEK cells model Niemann–Pick disease type C by developing enlarged, lipid-dense lysosomes, cholesterol and sphingolipid accumulation, and reduced mitochondria–lysosome contacts despite largely preserved mitochondrial respiration. HP-β-cyclodextrin cleared lysosomal cholesterol and normalized lysosomal morphology, while recombinant NPC2 reversed cholesterol accumulation and lysosomal enlargement, providing experimentally supported approaches for studying or clearing lysosomal storage.

papers.title: Rational design, preparation, and characterization of a therapeutic enzyme mutant with improved stability and function for cocaine detoxification.
papers.summary: The paper rationally engineered a cocaine esterase mutant, E196–301, by adding L196C/I301C substitutions that form cross-subunit disulfide bonds, thereby improving both thermal stability and catalytic activity against cocaine. PEGylated E196–301 retained activity and extended in vivo protection from lethal cocaine challenge in mice, supporting a transferable protein-design strategy for improving enzyme stability and function.

papers.title: Fluorescence polarisation activity-based protein profiling for the identification of deoxynojirimycin-type inhibitors selective for lysosomal retaining alpha- and beta-glucosidases.
papers.summary: The paper develops FluoPol-ABPP assays and identifies selective iminosugar inhibitors of lysosomal GAA, including compound 15, as lead scaffolds for pharmacological chaperone therapy in Pompe disease. The strategy uses competitive inhibitors to stabilize misfolded lysosomal enzymes and may transfer conceptually to Fabry disease, but this paper does not directly study alpha-galactosidase A or Fabry disease models.

papers.title: Improving the reversibility of thermal denaturation and catalytic efficiency of Bacillus licheniformis α-amylase through stabilizing a long loop in domain B.
papers.summary: Site-directed mutagenesis stabilized a long loop in Bacillus licheniformis α-amylase, with A269K/S187D/N188T improving thermal-denaturation reversibility ninefold and catalytic efficiency 1.84-fold relative to wild type. The study provides an indirect protein-engineering precedent, but it did not test alpha-galactosidase A, Fabry disease, chemical chaperones, or a lysosomal disease model.

papers.title: Study of the Structure-Function-Stability Relationships in Yeast D-amino Acid Oxidase: Hydrophobization of Alpha-Helices.
papers.summary: The study engineered stability and catalytic properties of recombinant D-amino acid oxidase from Trigonopsis variabilis by site-directed replacement of alpha-helical serine residues with alanine. Some substitutions, particularly S105A, improved thermal stability and catalytic efficiency, whereas others strongly destabilized the enzyme, showing that alpha-helix hydrophobization is a protein-specific exploratory strategy rather than a reliably transferable therapeutic approach.

papers.title: Fully automatized high-throughput enzyme library screening using a robotic platform.
papers.summary: The paper establishes a fully automated robotic platform for high-throughput production and screening of mutant enzyme libraries, including protein-stability tests and multiple assays. It does not study Fabry disease, GLA, alpha-galactosidase A, or the mechanism "alpha-galactosidase A physical stability," so it provides no direct evidence for transfer to Fabry disease.

papers.title: Identification of mutations in the alpha-L-iduronidase gene (IDUA) that cause Hurler and Scheie syndromes.
papers.summary: The paper identifies seven mutations in IDUA, including four previously undescribed mutations, that help explain biochemical and clinical variation in mucopolysaccharidosis type I (MPS-I). Expression of the R89Q variant demonstrated reduced stability and activity of alpha-L-iduronidase, providing a transferable model of unstable lysosomal glycosidase caused by a missense mutation; the paper does not directly study alpha-galactosidase A or Fabry disease.

unread.title: Anderson-Fabry disease cardiomyopathy: an update on epidemiology, diagnostic approach, management and monitoring strategies.
unread.why: This review reports approved Fabry therapies and established diagnostic, imaging, biomarker, and monitoring approaches with disease-specific clinical context.

unread.title: Complement activation and cellular inflammation in Fabry disease patients despite enzyme replacement therapy.
unread.why: The study provides Fabry-specific data showing complement and cytokine activation during ERT and identifies measurable inflammatory markers and a potential therapeutic target.

unread.title: Circulated TGF-β1 and VEGF-A as Biomarkers for Fabry Disease-Associated Cardiomyopathy.
unread.why: The study identifies circulating biomarkers associated with Fabry cardiomyopathy and early myocardial fibrosis, with potential prognostic value.

unread.title: Reducing agalsidase beta infusion time in Fabry patients: low incidence of antibody formation and infusion-associated reactions in an Italian multicenter study.
unread.why: This multicenter study directly validates a practical agalsidase beta administration protocol and reports immunogenicity, safety, and clinical outcomes.

unread.title: Genotype-Phenotype Correlations in 293 Russian Patients with Causal Fabry Disease Variants.
unread.why: The large cohort demonstrates an operational Fabry screening algorithm combining lyso-Gb3 testing with GLA sequencing and reports diagnostic and genotype-phenotype outcomes.

unread.title: Clinical Characteristics, Renal Involvement, and Therapeutic Options of Pediatric Patients With Fabry Disease.
unread.why: This review summarizes Fabry-specific renal treatments, nephroprotective drugs, laboratory monitoring, and urinary diagnostic approaches in pediatric disease.

unread.title: Agalsidase alfa--a preparation for enzyme replacement therapy in Anderson-Fabry disease.
unread.why: The review focuses on the clinical efficacy, safety, and tolerability of approved enzyme replacement preparations for Anderson-Fabry disease.

unread.title: Plain language summary of a study looking at heart muscle thickness and kidney function in women with Fabry disease who received agalsidase beta treatment.
unread.why: The registry-based longitudinal study reports outcomes associated with agalsidase beta treatment in women with Fabry disease.

unread.title: Characterization of Classical and Nonclassical Fabry Disease: A Multicenter Study.
unread.why: The multicenter study establishes clinically useful natural-history endpoints and phenotype-specific risk measures for Fabry disease.

unread.title: Newborn screening for Fabry disease in Taiwan reveals a high incidence of the later-onset GLA mutation c.936+919G>A (IVS4+919G>A).
unread.why: The pilot newborn-screening program demonstrates a diagnostic workflow for detecting Fabry disease and identifying prevalent GLA variants.

unread.title: The molecular defect leading to Fabry disease: structure of human alpha-galactosidase.
unread.why: The paper provides a structural and catalytic reference for alpha-galactosidase A that can support mutation interpretation and therapeutic design in Fabry disease.

unread.title: Effects of a chemical chaperone on genetic mutations in alpha-galactosidase A in Korean patients with Fabry disease.
unread.why: DGJ is experimentally shown to enhance GLA activity and expression in cells carrying milder Fabry disease mutations.

unread.title: Diagnostic strategy for females suspected of Fabry disease.
unread.why: The large female cohort shows that combining enzyme activity with Lyso-Gb3 substantially improves diagnostic detection and positive predictive value.

unread.title: Diagnosis of Fabry Disease Using Alpha-Galactosidase A Activity or LysoGb3 in Blood Fails to Identify Up to Two Thirds of Female Patients.
unread.why: The study identifies major diagnostic limitations of blood enzyme and LysoGb3 testing in females and supports genetic confirmation.

unread.title: Renoprotective Effect of Agalsidase Alfa: A Long-Term Follow-Up of Patients with Fabry Disease.
unread.why: The long-term registry analysis reports renal outcomes associated with agalsidase alfa and identifies baseline proteinuria as an important prognostic factor.

unread.title: Impact of enzyme replacement therapy and migalastat on left atrial strain and cardiomyopathy in patients with Fabry disease.
unread.why: This longitudinal Fabry cohort shows stable left atrial strain and left ventricular mass during enzyme replacement or chaperone therapy and validates strain echocardiography as an outcome measure.

unread.title: Importance of Echocardiography and Clinical "Red Flags" in Guiding Genetic Screening for Fabry Disease.
unread.why: The study validates a targeted screening workflow for Fabry disease in patients with unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy and phenotypic red flags, including familial detection.

unread.title: Fabry disease Enzyme Enhancement on migalastat Study: FEES.
unread.why: The study quantifies migalastat-associated enzyme enhancement and supports dried blood spot lyso-Gb3 as a feasible disease-monitoring marker in Fabry patients.

unread.title: The gatekeeper images in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: the role of native T1 mapping in Anderson-Fabry disease.
unread.why: The case provides direct evidence that reduced native myocardial T1 on cardiac MRI can serve as a gatekeeper imaging feature for differentiating Anderson-Fabry disease from other hypertrophic cardiomyopathies.

unread.title: Effects of enzyme replacement therapy on the cardiomyopathy of Anderson-Fabry disease: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial of agalsidase alfa.
unread.why: This randomized placebo-controlled trial provides direct evidence that agalsidase alfa reduces myocardial Gb3 and left ventricular mass and regresses Fabry-associated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

unread.title: Detection of single nucleotide and copy number variants in the Fabry disease-associated GLA gene using nanopore sequencing.
unread.why: The paper validates a cost-effective long-read assay that detected Fabry-associated missense, deep-intronic, and copy-number GLA variants, including a deletion missed by Sanger sequencing.

unread.title: The Benefits of Family Screening in Rare Diseases: Genetic Testing Reveals 165 New Cases of Fabry Disease among At-Risk Family Members of 83 Index Patients.
unread.why: The study demonstrates cascade genotyping in 331 relatives, identifying 165 additional Fabry cases and supporting a reusable family-screening workflow.

unread.title: Systematic cascade screening in the Danish Fabry Disease Centre: 20 years of a national single-centre experience.
unread.why: Twenty years of nationwide cascade testing produced a registered Fabry cohort, six newly identified pathogenic variants, and earlier diagnosis among family members.

unread.title: Assessment and impact of dose escalation on anti-drug antibodies in Fabry disease.
unread.why: The study provides assays and longitudinal data showing how anti-drug antibody measurement, titration, lyso-Gb3 monitoring, and dose escalation can guide enzyme replacement therapy.

unread.title: Plasma Globotriaosylsphingosine and α-Galactosidase A Activity as a Combined Screening Biomarker for Fabry Disease in a Large Japanese Cohort.
unread.why: A 5,691-patient Japanese study validates a combined biochemical screening strategy for classic and late-onset Fabry disease.

unread.title: Correlation of retinal vascular characteristics with laboratory and ocular findings in Fabry disease: exploring ocular diagnostic biomarkers.
unread.why: The prospective case-control study identifies OCTA-derived retinal vascular measurements and cornea verticillata as candidate indicators of Fabry activity, diagnosis, and progression.

unread.title: Magnitude of the Potential Screening Gap for Fabry Disease in Manitoba: A Population-Based Retrospective Cohort Study.
unread.why: The study demonstrates how population administrative data can identify people with high-risk phenotypes for targeted GLA testing and quantify the Fabry screening gap.

unread.title: Use of T1 mapping in cardiac MRI for the follow-up of Fabry disease in a pediatric population.
unread.why: Longitudinal pediatric Fabry data show that noninvasive cardiac MRI T1 mapping can characterize early myocardial involvement and monitor response to ERT.

unread.title: A Meta-Analysis to Unveil the Diagnostic Gaps in Anderson-Fabry Disease in Women.
unread.why: Meta-analysis of 67 studies directly supports GLA genetic testing as a more sensitive diagnostic strategy than enzyme-only testing in women with unexplained cardiac, renal, or cerebrovascular events.

unread.title: What Is the Role of Sensorineural Hearing Loss in Fabry Disease Screening?
unread.why: Screening 168 patients with idiopathic hearing loss using enzyme activity and GLA testing diagnosed two Fabry cases and identified additional relatives through cascade screening.

unread.title: A phase 4, open-label, multicenter study of the safety and efficacy of agalsidase beta in Chinese patients with Fabry disease.
unread.why: A multicenter phase 4 study directly evaluates agalsidase beta safety and biochemical, renal, and clinical efficacy in Chinese patients with Fabry disease.

unread.title: Urinary VEGF-A165b mRNA expression in Fabry disease: Pilot study.
unread.why: The pilot study establishes a urinary RT-qPCR assay for VEGF-A165b mRNA as an exploratory nephropathy biomarker and reports its association with ERT duration.

unread.title: From Shoulder to Heart: Acute Shoulder Pain Leads to a Diagnosis of Fabry Disease.
unread.why: The case supplies a concrete diagnostic work-up and reports initiation of migalastat after late-onset Fabry disease was confirmed.

unread.title: A diagnostic challenge of advanced-stage cardiac Fabry disease without left ventricular hypertrophy: a case report.
unread.why: The report identifies wall thinning, fatty infiltration, fibrosis, and multimodal cardiac imaging as diagnostic clues for advanced cardiac Fabry disease without left ventricular hypertrophy.

unread.title: Early mitophagy defects and impaired mitochondrial energy metabolism drive target organ damage progression: lessons from the Fabry heart.
unread.why: Using a humanized Fabry mouse model and derived cells, the study shows that L-arginine-mediated mitochondrial rescue prevents cardiac abnormalities.

unread.title: Effectiveness and tolerability of migalastat in adult Fabry disease: A single regional centre experience.
unread.why: Real-world data from 87 adults provide genotype-stratified safety, biochemical, renal, and cardiac evidence for migalastat.

unread.title: Generation of human induced pluripotent stem cell line MHHi040-A from a female Fabry disease patient carrying c.644A>G missense mutation.
unread.why: The validated patient-derived iPSC line carrying GLA c.644A>G is a reusable model for Fabry disease mechanisms and therapeutic screening.

unread.title: Enzyme replacement therapy for Anderson-Fabry disease.
unread.why: A systematic review of five randomized trials provides direct comparative evidence for the biochemical and clinical effects of agalsidase alfa and beta in Fabry disease.

unread.title: [Anderson-Fabry disease].
unread.why: The article identifies two approved enzyme replacement products for Fabry disease, although the abstract is primarily descriptive.

unread.title: Anderson – Fabry Disease Homozygosity: Rare Case of Late-Onset Variant
unread.why: The case provides patient-specific evidence for targeted GLA-variant screening and treatment with migalastat or agalsidase beta and identifies a long-term migalastat registry.

unread.title: Venglustat, an orally administered glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor: Assessment over 3 years in adult males with classic Fabry disease in an open-label phase 2 study and its extension study.
unread.why: The three-year study provides clinical and pharmacodynamic evidence that oral venglustat reduces glycosphingolipid biomarkers and measures of cutaneous GL-3 accumulation.

unread.title: Establishment of Cutoff Values for Newborn Screening of Six Lysosomal Storage Disorders by Tandem Mass Spectrometry.
unread.why: The study validates an MS/MS newborn-screening workflow and reports a batch-relative GLA activity cutoff that identified infants subsequently diagnosed with Fabry disease.

unread.title: Biomarkers for Monitoring Renal Damage Due to Fabry Disease in Patients Treated with Migalastat: A Review for Nephrologists.
unread.why: The review identifies creatinine-based eGFR as the principal supported renal biomarker for monitoring Fabry nephropathy during migalastat treatment.

unread.title: A Kidney Transplant Recipient Treated With Migalastat for Fabry Disease for 33 Months.
unread.why: The case demonstrates post-transplant genetic identification of Fabry disease and 33 months of stable clinical outcomes with migalastat for an amenable GLA variant.

unread.title: The pharmacological chaperone 1-deoxygalactonojirimycin increases alpha-galactosidase A levels in Fabry patient cell lines.
unread.why: The study tests migalastat in Fabry patient-derived cells, identifies responsive GLA mutants, and shows increased enzyme activity and reduced GL-3 accumulation.

unread.title: Migalastat HCl reduces globotriaosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb3) in Fabry transgenic mice and in the plasma of Fabry patients.
unread.why: The study demonstrated migalastat-mediated substrate reduction in Fabry mice and patients while validating a quantitative lyso-Gb3 LC-MS/MS assay.

unread.title: Safety and efficacy of pegunigalsidase alfa in patients with Fabry disease who were previously treated with agalsidase alfa: results from BRIDGE, a phase 3 open-label study.
unread.why: A phase 3 switch study showed that pegunigalsidase alfa was generally safe and reduced plasma lyso-Gb3 while stabilizing eGFR decline in previously treated adults with Fabry disease.

unread.title: Prevalence of Fabry Disease in Young Patients with Stroke in Argentina.
unread.why: The study implemented enzyme and genetic screening in young stroke/TIA patients and demonstrated its diagnostic yield and utility for distinguishing benign GLA variants.

unread.title: Results of an ophthalmologic screening programme for identification of cases with Anderson-Fabry disease.
unread.why: The screening program confirmed one previously undiagnosed case and provides an ophthalmic case-finding strategy for Fabry disease.

unread.title: Nationwide screening for Fabry disease in unselected stroke patients.
unread.why: A nationwide prospective screen established a stepwise diagnostic workflow and identified pathogenic Fabry disease in previously unrecognized stroke patients.

unread.title: Prevalence of Anderson-Fabry disease in a cohort with unexplained late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI.
unread.why: Testing patients with otherwise unexplained mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement identified Fabry disease in 2.5% of the selected cohort, supporting MRI-triggered screening.

unread.title: Safety and efficacy of migalastat in adolescent patients with Fabry disease: Results from ASPIRE, a phase 3b, open-label, single-arm, 12-month clinical trial, and its open-label extension.
unread.why: The ASPIRE study and extension provide longitudinal safety, pharmacodynamic, organ-function, pain, and quality-of-life data for migalastat in adolescents with amenable GLA variants.

unread.title: [Clinical features and enzyme replacement therapy in 4 children with Fabry disease].
unread.why: This small pediatric case series reports tolerability of agalsidase beta and short-term improvement in neuropathic pain and hypohidrosis in children with Fabry disease.

unread.title: Pathogenicity of novel GLA gene missense mutations in Fabry disease and the therapeutic impact of migalastat.
unread.why: The study functionally validates novel GLA variants in mutant HEK293 cells and shows that migalastat restores alpha-Gal A expression and activity for a newly identified amenable variant.

unread.title: Challenges in Fabry disease: the combination of two individually amenable GLA variants may be nonamenable to migalastat.
unread.why: This Fabry case demonstrates that a validated in vitro GLA variant assay can identify patients whose two-variant combination is unexpectedly nonamenable to migalastat and informs therapeutic selection.

unread.title: Late-onset renal variant Fabry disease with R112H mutation and mild increase in plasma globotriaosylsphingosine: a case report.
unread.why: The case reports approximately 10 years of treatment with agalsidase beta followed by migalastat in Fabry disease and provides evidence for lyso-Gb3 normalization and renal stabilization.

unread.title: Investigating undiagnosed Fabry disease in young adults with ischemic stroke: A multicenter cohort study.
unread.why: This multicenter cohort develops and applies a screening workflow for undiagnosed Fabry disease in young adults with ischemic stroke or TIA using enzyme activity, lyso-Gb3, and GLA sequencing.

unread.title: Impact of migalastat on cerebral outcomes in fabry disease - results from the prospective observational FAMOUS trial.
unread.why: The prospective FAMOUS analysis reports cerebral MRI outcomes during migalastat treatment and shows largely stable white-matter lesion load while identifying hypertension as a potential modifier.

unread.title: Lucerastat, an oral therapy for Fabry disease: results from a pivotal randomized phase 3 study and its open-label extension.
unread.why: The phase 3 MODIFY study provides direct evidence that oral lucerastat lowers plasma Gb3 but does not significantly improve neuropathic pain, while also characterizing renal and safety outcomes.

unread.title: Limited effects of long-term enzyme replacement therapy on the cardiac conduction system in Fabry disease.
unread.why: This Fabry case provides longitudinal evidence that long-term ERT may not prevent advanced atrioventricular block and reports the use of a pacemaker for severe conduction disease.

unread.title: Fabry disease, an under-recognized multisystemic disorder: expert recommendations for diagnosis, management, and enzyme replacement therapy.
unread.why: This expert review summarizes clinical-trial and disease-management evidence supporting recombinant alpha-galactosidase A ERT and early initiation in Fabry disease.

unread.title: Treatment of Fabry's Disease with the Pharmacologic Chaperone Migalastat.
unread.why: This randomized trial directly evaluates migalastat in variant-suitable Fabry disease and reports renal, cardiac, substrate, safety, and patient-reported outcomes.

unread.title: Agalsidase-beta therapy for advanced Fabry disease: a randomized trial.
unread.why: The randomized trial provides direct Fabry disease evidence for agalsidase beta delaying clinical progression in advanced disease, with quantified renal, cardiac, and cerebrovascular outcomes.

unread.title: Fabry disease: detection of undiagnosed hemodialysis patients and identification of a "renal variant" phenotype.
unread.why: The study reports an effective screening strategy for undiagnosed Fabry disease among hemodialysis patients and identifies a clinically distinct renal variant.

unread.title: Improvement of cardiac function during enzyme replacement therapy in patients with Fabry disease: a prospective strain rate imaging study.
unread.why: This prospective clinical study provides outcome data and a quantitative strain-imaging method for assessing cardiac improvement during agalsidase beta ERT in Fabry disease.

unread.title: Cardiac manifestations of Anderson-Fabry disease: results from the international Fabry outcome survey.
unread.why: Large multicenter Fabry cohort data characterize cardiac outcomes and monitor long-term efficacy and safety of agalsidase alfa.

unread.title: The Mainz Severity Score Index: a new instrument for quantifying the Anderson-Fabry disease phenotype, and the response of patients to enzyme replacement therapy.
unread.why: The MSSI is a disease-specific severity instrument validated in Fabry patients and shown to decline after agalsidase alfa treatment.

unread.title: High incidence of the cardiac variant of Fabry disease revealed by newborn screening in the Taiwan Chinese population.
unread.why: Large-scale newborn and cardiomyopathy screening demonstrates an effective diagnostic workflow for identifying cardiac-variant Fabry disease early.

unread.title: Prevalence of Fabry disease in female patients with late-onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
unread.why: The study validates biochemical, genetic, and tissue-based approaches for diagnosing Fabry disease in women with late-onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

unread.title: Newborn screening for six lysosomal storage disorders in a cohort of Mexican patients: Three-year findings from a screening program in a closed Mexican health system.
unread.why: A large Mexican newborn cohort demonstrated the feasibility of detecting Fabry disease alongside five other lysosomal disorders using a multiplex DBS enzyme assay.

unread.title: A comprehensive testing algorithm for the diagnosis of Fabry disease in males and females.
unread.why: The study validated a diagnostic algorithm in 294 at-risk patients and showed that plasma lyso-Gb3 plus GLA sequencing provided high diagnostic performance in both sexes.

unread.title: Clinical observation of patients with Fabry disease after switching from agalsidase beta (Fabrazyme) to agalsidase alfa (Replagal).
unread.why: Eleven patients remained stable after switching from agalsidase beta to agalsidase alfa, with longitudinal renal, cardiac, pain, quality-of-life, and safety data.

unread.title: Lysosomal storage disorder 4+1 multiplex assay for newborn screening using tandem mass spectrometry: application to a small-scale population study for five lysosomal storage disorders.
unread.why: The optimized high-throughput newborn-screening assay was evaluated in 5,055 newborns and reliably distinguished Fabry disease controls from normal specimens.

unread.title: Long-term follow-up of renal function in patients treated with migalastat for Fabry disease.
unread.why: Provides long-term efficacy data for migalastat in amenable-variant Fabry disease and establishes a quantitative renal outcome measure.

unread.title: The Large Phenotypic Spectrum of Fabry Disease Requires Graduated Diagnosis and Personalized Therapy: A Meta-Analysis Can Help to Differentiate Missense Mutations.
unread.why: Reviews tested pharmacological chaperones and summarizes cell-based enzyme measurements for selecting GLA variants responsive to chaperone therapy.

unread.title: Results of Fabry Disease Screening in Male Pre-End Stage Renal Disease Patients with Unknown Etiology Found Through the Platform of a Chronic Kidney Disease Education Program in a Northern Taiwan Medical Center.
unread.why: Validates a high-risk CKD screening workflow that identified previously unrecognized Fabry disease cases and also documents a false-negative result.

unread.title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing in Fabry disease.
unread.why: Shows that cardiopulmonary exercise testing detects an exercise-related blood-pressure abnormality associated with impaired exercise tolerance in Fabry disease.

unread.title: Prognostic significance of right ventricular hypertrophy and systolic function in Anderson-Fabry disease.
unread.why: Longitudinal Fabry data evaluate echocardiographic and renal measures as predictors of major cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and renal outcomes.

unread.title: Genomic screening of Fabry disease in young stroke patients: the Taiwan experience and a review of the literature.
unread.why: Tests a genetic screening assay in 1,000 young stroke patients and detects a recurrent Fabry-associated GLA variant in affected males.

unread.title: Oxidative stress biomarkers in Fabry disease: is there a room for them?
unread.why: Measured blood oxidative-stress biomarkers in Fabry patients and found abnormalities in treated and untreated disease, supporting their potential as early markers.
